[Current account](SPR-L1.md) · [Complete scientific fields](SPR-L1-CURRENT-PROPERTIES.json) · [Sources and limits](SOURCES.md#spr-l1)

This is the separate current population of 83 native rows. Original and corrected identities are retained. Retention status, applicability and evaluated truth are different fields. The JSON companion includes every scientific property field and its attribute/predicate/profile records.

**Evidence limit:** these available ledger bytes do not recover the original final r4 subject, certificate or review pair, or the currently unavailable complete r4 candidate.

Both available 83-row populations also carry the same [earlier ledger-recorded canonical review history](SPR-L1-RECORDED-REVIEW-HISTORY.md). Its complete object is [preserved once](SPR-L1-RECORDED-REVIEW-HISTORY.json) and referenced from every structured property row. That historical packet-level scope and its explanation of inherited author-stage wording do not recover or substitute for the missing original r4 proof or complete r4 candidate.

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Gold 1967 formalizes learning in the limit and distinguishes positive text from informant presentations.

**Original terminology.** identification in the limit; text; informant; superfinite class

**Original form.** Given indefinitely accumulating accepted strings, infer every target language exactly without negative evidence or restrictive class conditions.

**Original problem.** Finite successful observations never by themselves exclude an overgeneral language.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RBR0018

**Influence or relation class.** Source-specific documented ancestry where cited; operational predicate and cross-domain constraint are present analytical reconstruction, not claimed historical wording.

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** ESI-RS0063

**Locators.** Table I p.452; §8 p.460; §9 pp.460–461

**Claim supported.** For superfinite language classes, arbitrary positive text does not permit universal eventual exact identification; restricted presentations/classes have different limits.

**Role.** Direct result/case or bounded complementary limit; consult source access level. Multiple references are not independent replications.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0064

**Locators.** §1.1 pp.88–89, teacher; §1.2 pp.88–89, practicality; §2.1 pp.90–91, closed/consistent table; Theorem6 p.97

**Claim supported.** L* obtains the minimal DFA under correct membership and equivalence queries; its original discussion explicitly questions practical equivalence access.

**Role.** Direct result/case or bounded complementary limit; consult source access level. Multiple references are not independent replications.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0065

**Locators.** Introduction pp.1–2; Definition1 pp.2–3; discussion of optimistic merges and characteristic data

**Claim supported.** Characteristic labeled data and ordering assumptions govern passive state-merging identification; a finite arbitrary sample is not automatically characteristic.

**Role.** Direct result/case or bounded complementary limit; consult source access level. Multiple references are not independent replications.

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not retroactively name every source Evolved System Identification or assert that all branches descend from control. Gold 1967 formalizes learning in the limit and distinguishes positive text from informant presentations.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Reject universal eventual exact identification of a superfinite language class from arbitrary positive text. Preserve the distinct, warranted practice of stating the class, presentation, equivalence and success quantifiers; restricted positive-only results are not rejected.

**Claim class.** NEGATIVE_RESULT_AND_RESEARCHER_OPERATIONALIZATION

**Bearer or subject.** A language-learning problem (target class, evidence presentation, learner, equivalence and convergence criterion).

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Finite successful observations never by themselves exclude an overgeneral language.

**Mechanism.** Gold’s impossibility addresses all learners and admissible positive presentations in the stated class. A finite pair of compatible languages illustrates finite ambiguity but is not itself the proof of nonidentification in the limit.

**Mature or evolved form.** The negative candidate and its accurate-limit assessment remain explicit. Positive-only observations leave unobserved strings unlabeled. A retains the universal negative as its own claim. B0025 supplies a broader positive rule and is a near-neighbor, not a replacement or duplicate.

**Expected payoff.** Prevents an unsupported unique machine from being mistaken for an identified target; directs acquisition toward genuinely distinguishing evidence.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Mathematical impossibility, not an empirical productivity effect: Gold Table I and §9. Positive-only finite-language classes provide a boundary to the negative claim.

**Decision or consumer.** Researcher or engineer deciding whether a unique learned behavior is supportable.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Informant data; exact or approximate active queries; prior restriction of target class; prediction on a bounded input distribution; retain multiple compatible candidates.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** An exact or eventual-general recovery assertion invokes arbitrary positive text over an unrestricted superfinite class; a finite trace summary with no such assertion is outside this negative claim.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known finite target alternatives with a proven distinguishing presentation, or a task requiring only a finite observed-trace summary.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** The negative theorem uses arbitrary positive texts and eventual exact identification of each member; altered probability, presentation or target class requires separate analysis.

**Environment and boundary.** Languages of strings; deployed state/time semantics are outside the theorem unless represented and justified.

**Scope and exclusions.** Universal eventual convergence for every target and admissible text is different from finite consistency and from a learner knowing when it has converged. Retain the criticism of positive-only universal recovery without turning it into a claim that every restricted positive-only learner fails.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** No normative requirement is derived; this is a limit on descriptive inference.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Keep accepted examples, evidence presentation contract, allowed target class and the precise output equivalence criterion.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Canonical consequence.** Links to BH02 and BH03 as information-changing alternatives. Neither extra notation nor richer states alone supplies missing discriminating evidence.

**Input conditions.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0201

**Original value.** Active queries C0202 can change information access; richer representations C0203 change the class but do not erase in distinguish ability.

**Failure of assumptions.** If presentation is characteristic or probabilistic ally restricted, the quoted impossibility may no longer apply; do not overextend it.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Enumerating all alternatives is generally unnecessary; a small counterexample pair can refute an unjustified uniqueness claim.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-enter if negative evidence, oracle access or target-class restriction changes; do not carry old impossibility unchanged into a new problem.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0028

**Strongest objection.** Retain the criticism of positive-only universal recovery without turning it into a claim that every restricted positive-only learner fails.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: declaring a+ uniquely recovered from {a, aa} fails because {a, aa} remains consistent.

**Response or descendant form.** Active querying and labeled characteristic data change the problem’s information, not the truth of the original negative result.

**What changed and what did not.** The negative candidate and its accurate-limit assessment remain explicit. Positive-only observations leave unobserved strings unlabeled. A retains the universal negative as its own claim. B0025 supplies a broader positive rule and is a near-neighbor, not a replacement or duplicate.

**Residual limits.** For a concrete restricted class, determine its presentation promise and actual theorem; the present rejection does not decide that new problem.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A named theorem is useful only if its class and quantifiers match; attaching “Gold impossibility” to every inference task is a ceremonial veto.

**Internal tension ids.** None recorded.

**Retention status.** REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED

**Retention rationale.** Reject universal eventual exact identification of a superfinite language class from arbitrary positive text. Preserve the distinct, warranted practice of stating the class, presentation, equivalence and success quantifiers; restricted positive-only results are not rejected. A:C002 reads the result table and discussion; B:BH001 separately inspected theorem I.8 visually. These are access events for Gold’s same work, not two replications. A:C004 is the 1996 characterization work, not the original 1992 RPNI paper.

**Assumptions.** The negative theorem uses arbitrary positive texts and eventual exact identification of each member; altered probability, presentation or target class requires separate analysis.

**Applicability guard.** An exact/general reconstruction claim is based only on accepted traces with an unrestricted superfinite candidate class.

**Expression or precise operational rule.** If class is superfinite, presentation is arbitrary positive text, and claim is eventual exact identification for every class member, mark that recovery claim unsupported and retain ambiguity. PASS means this limit is represented accurately; FAIL means universal recovery is asserted; UNKNOWN means class/presentation are unspecified; INAPPLICABLE means no general exact-recovery claim.

**Source of the expression.** **Type.** RESEARCHER_OPERATIONALIZATION

**Rationale.** Operational rule derived from the source-supported limit/mechanism; not claimed as a verbatim theorem or universally mandatory process.

**Source ids.** ESI-RS0063; ESI-RS0064; ESI-RS0065

**Observation or measurement map.** Keep accepted examples, evidence presentation contract, allowed target class and the precise output equivalence criterion.

**Required evidence.** Formal problem statement and domain restriction, challenged with alternative targets.; Inspect data-generation contract; distinguish accepted-only log from explicit negative labels.; Keep accepted examples, evidence presentation contract, allowed target class and the precise output equivalence criterion.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** First establish applicability. Inspect the two attributes and source witnesses; challenge the claim using the negative example; determine whether the stated supported condition, an actual breach, or unresolved evidence is present. Apply the explicit outcome semantics below.

**Decidability and approximation.** Qualified impossibility and constructed ambiguity; no blanket impossibility of useful inference or human language learning. The operational review is evidence-bounded; it must not claim a complete decision procedure beyond the selected model/theorem.

**Positive witness.** Constructed: observations {a, aa} fit both finite language {a, aa} and a+. Recording both and withholding unique recovery passes the evidential limit.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** Constructed: declaring a+ uniquely recovered from {a, aa} fails because {a, aa} remains consistent.

**Unknown conditions.** Which restricted classes and observation regimes fit a particular task remains target-dependent. Also unknown when a load-bearing field is missing or assumptions cannot be checked.

**Inapplicability conditions.** Known finite target alternatives with a proven distinguishing presentation, or a task requiring only a finite observed-trace summary.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** Treating a restrictive sample promise as arbitrary text can falsely reject a valid restricted result.

**False negative.** Failing to recognize an implicit superfinite hypothesis class can allow an impossible universal promise.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Stating “bounded model” without specifying the allowed alternatives hides the unrestricted premise.

**Change invalidation rule.** A change in class, presentation, oracle or success criterion invalidates the prior learnability judgment.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Enumerating all alternatives is generally unnecessary; a small counterexample pair can refute an unjustified uniqueness claim. Cheaper route: Informant data; exact or approximate active queries; prior restriction of target class; prediction on a bounded input distribution; retain multiple compatible candidates.

**Evidence ceiling.** Qualified impossibility and constructed ambiguity; no blanket impossibility of useful inference or human language learning.

**Evaluation outcomes.** **Pass.** The precise scoped operational rule is satisfied with sufficient stated evidence; does not imply stronger truth, universality or adoption.

**Fail.** A valid witness or directly established mismatch contradicts that operational rule in its applicable context.

**Unknown.** The guard may apply but evidence, mapping, premise or computation is insufficient; this is neither pass nor logical negation.

**Inapplicable.** The declared guard is false; use the named non-trigger route rather than treating absence as failure.

**Evaluated proposition.** Warranted reporting of the positive-text identification limit, not truth of universal recovery

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Angluin 1987 distinguishes exact equivalence from sampling; Vaandrager–Melse2025 develops larger conformance fault domains.

**Original terminology.** Equivalence query, counterexample, m-complete and k-A-complete test suite

**Original form.** A practical tester returns no counterexample after finite testing but the learner interface calls this equivalence.

**Original problem.** A practical tester returns no counterexample after finite testing but the learner interface calls this equivalence.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RGN0280

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Claim.** Exact equivalence and sampling are distinct.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0111

**Locator.** §1.2 and Theorem7

**Claim.** No unrestricted finite suite; conditional Wp/HSI guarantee and counterexamples for other methods.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0136

**Locator.** Introduction and k-A completeness results

**Claim.** Practical protocol tests are budgeted and harness-bound.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0120

**Locator.** §3 and Table2

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** The candidate wording is a present synthesis. Named native terms retain their original scope; no claim that all branches descend from continuous control. Nondeterministic ioco and stochastic distribution comparison require different semantics; Mealy completeness is not portable unchanged.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A callback or successful test suite provides only its specified answer semantics. An exact-equivalence conclusion from conformance testing requires the actual abstract target to belong to the same fault domain for which the suite is complete.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_ENGINEERING_MECHANISM

**Bearer or subject.** Mealy machines H,M; fault domain F; finite suite T; observation map a

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A practical tester returns no counterexample after finite testing but the learner interface calls this equivalence.

**Mechanism.** For output abstraction a, let M_a=a(M). If M_a belongs to F_a and T is F_a-complete for H, agreement of H and M_a on every w in T warrants H≡M_a. Raw-target membership M∈F or raw completeness alone cannot discharge abstract premises.

**Mature or evolved form.** A’s oracle-contract facet and B’s conformance distinction both forbid promoting no counterexample found into an exact oracle answer. A retains exact membership/equivalence, trusted-equivalence noisy-membership variants and practical query constraints. B adds the 2025 fault-domain theorem and the corrected common-abstract-domain requirement. Initial-state evidence goes to BH04.

**Expected payoff.** Makes the stopping claim defensible and directs testing toward distinctions the current hypothesis omits.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Unrestricted finite-suite impossibility and k-A completeness/counterexamples are proved in BH027; TLS uses practical bounded tests. These support conditional validity, not a universal test budget.

**Decision or consumer.** A model-learning consumer deciding whether a hypothesis is adequate for testing, verification or deployment analysis.

**Alternative mechanisms.** For bug finding, one replayed counterexample may answer the decision without proving full equivalence; see C0042.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A learner invokes an oracle-dependent guarantee or declares success because an equivalence callback or conformance suite found no counterexample.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** For bug finding, one replayed counterexample may answer the decision without proving full equivalence; see C0042.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Known common input alphabet, output semantics and initial/reset convention; a defines a deterministic complete abstract machine of the required class; target M_a belongs to F_a and T is complete for H relative to F_a. If abstraction changes these conditions, prove a corresponding transport before using the theorem.

**Environment and boundary.** Finite input traces over the specified abstraction and implementation version; no claim over unmodeled timing, clients or data relations.

**Scope and exclusions.** Exact equivalence is universal over the selected behavior domain. A finite suite establishes finite agreement; it entails full equivalence only under the stated fault-domain completeness theorem. Sampling errors remain distribution-relative. Preserve approximate-oracle, class-bound and observation-abstraction objections. The packet’s corrected abstraction counterexample is a construction, not evidence of a deployed defect.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conformance to a learned hypothesis is descriptive. Conformance to an intended specification additionally requires an authoritative specification.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** **Claim links.** **Claim.** Exact equivalence and sampling are distinct.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0029; ESI-RCR0072

**Strongest objection.** Preserve approximate-oracle, class-bound and observation-abstraction objections. The packet’s corrected abstraction counterexample is a construction, not evidence of a deployed defect.

**Known failures and misuses.** CONSTRUCTED from BH027 argument: machine M matches every tested prefix up to maximum length N and changes its output after N+1 repetitions; it defeats unrestricted finite-test equivalence. Unknown state/access bound is treated as established, or finite random testing is reported as an exact teacher.

**Response or descendant form.** 2025 k-A domains relax crude state-count assumptions, but preserve an explicit reachability/access-sequence premise.

**What changed and what did not.** A’s oracle-contract facet and B’s conformance distinction both forbid promoting no counterexample found into an exact oracle answer. A retains exact membership/equivalence, trusted-equivalence noisy-membership variants and practical query constraints. B adds the 2025 fault-domain theorem and the corrected common-abstract-domain requirement. Initial-state evidence goes to BH04.

**Residual limits.** Obtain evidence of actual target membership in the abstract fault domain and the exact suite’s completeness. Inaccessible premises leave the stronger conclusion UNKNOWN, not false by default.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** For bug finding, one replayed counterexample may answer the decision without proving full equivalence; see C0042. Actual mechanism: For deterministic complete Mealy specification H and implementation M in fault domain F, use an F-complete suite T: agreement on T implies equivalence. Without M∈F, preserve finite-test status or a distributional guarantee.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0011; ESI-RTN0024; ESI-RTN0025

**Retention status.** STRONGLY_RETAINED

**Retention rationale.** A callback or successful test suite provides only its specified answer semantics. An exact-equivalence conclusion from conformance testing requires the actual abstract target to belong to the same fault domain for which the suite is complete. A:C003/B:BH002 are the same L* work with distinct inspected portions. B:BH027 is the primary 2025 fault-domain result. A:C032 assumes always-correct equivalence despite noisy membership; A:C005 is TTT abstract-only.

**Decidability and approximation.** Strong necessity of matching assumptions to claims; exact learning only under the theorem’s contract, not generic production completeness. The operational review is evidence-bounded; it must not claim a complete decision procedure beyond the selected model/theorem.

**Positive witness.** Constructed: a finite model oracle answers equality exactly and returns a replayable symmetric-difference string; theorem claim matches this access.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** Constructed: a random tester finds no failure in10,000 steps and the tool labels the hypothesis “equivalent”; exact identification is falsely asserted.

**Unknown conditions.** How to obtain sufficiently discriminating and affordable counterexamples for a particular live system. Also unknown when a load-bearing field is missing or assumptions cannot be checked.

**Inapplicability conditions.** A manually recorded trace is presented solely as that trace, with no generalized model or teacher guarantee.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** A deterministic test double can hide nondeterminism or durable-state leakage in deployment.

**False negative.** Demanding a reset when a proved homing/trace method suffices rejects a legitimate alternate regime.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Renaming an incomplete tester “exact” or silently excluding failed resets games the contract.

**Change invalidation rule.** Subject drift, durable-state leakage, changed abstraction, oracle strategy or budget reopens the contract.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Reset and counterexample searches may dominate cost; smaller discrimination structures reduce storage without making EQ free. Cheaper route: Passive characteristic data; direct property testing; homing/synchronization approach with its own assumptions; bounded model used only descriptively.

**Evidence ceiling.** Strong necessity of matching assumptions to claims; exact learning only under the theorem’s contract, not generic production completeness.

**Evaluation outcomes.** **Pass.** The precise scoped operational rule is satisfied with sufficient stated evidence; does not imply stronger truth, universality or adoption.

**Fail.** A valid witness or directly established mismatch contradicts that operational rule in its applicable context.

**Unknown.** The guard may apply but evidence, mapping, premise or computation is insufficient; this is neither pass nor logical negation.

**Inapplicable.** The declared guard is false; use the named non-trigger route rather than treating absence as failure.

**Evaluated proposition.** Broad claim-to-query-contract fidelity, oracle facet only; initial-state facet is BH04

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Angluin-style active learning presupposes repeatable membership access; Rivest–Schapire 1989 studies learning without reset.

**Original terminology.** Reset, homing sequence, strong connectivity, output query

**Original form.** Replaying an input word may start from a different hidden state or return timing-dependent observations.

**Original problem.** Replaying an input word may start from a different hidden state or return timing-dependent observations.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RGN0280

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Claim.** Strong connectivity and homing replace reset under a conditional probabilistic theorem.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0112

**Locator.** §2 and §4

**Claim.** Concrete protocol harness reset and timeout decisions.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0120

**Locator.** §3.1

**Claim.** Stochastic learner still requires step/reset interface.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0135

**Locator.** §3.4.1

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** The candidate wording is a present synthesis. Named native terms retain their original scope; no claim that all branches descend from continuous control. A reset-free finite strongly connected automaton result does not guarantee recovery of unreachable transient components.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Repeated words support a repeatable-state learning contract only when initial-state restoration or the specified state-revisitation mechanism and the observation mapping are justified.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_ENGINEERING_MECHANISM

**Bearer or subject.** learner L, query harness Q, reset/homing contract R, observation map a, replay evidence E

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Replaying an input word may start from a different hidden state or return timing-dependent observations.

**Mechanism.** Separate process, session, account and environment state; record resetting, homing or other revisitation assumptions, and distinguish observed replay agreement from a universal restoration guarantee.

**Mature or evolved form.** A’s initial-state evidence and B’s lifecycle/replay treatment identify the same failure: nominally repeated words can start from different states. B separates lifecycle contract from observed replay consistency. Homing under strong connectivity and a counterexample teacher is a conditional substitute for reset, not free reset. A’s oracle correctness remains BH03.

**Expected payoff.** Prevents inconsistent query tables and false state distinctions caused by hidden session carryover or timing.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Reset-free learning is proved for specified finite-state access; TLS demonstrates fresh-process/socket handling. Neither proves all services are resettable or safely homed.

**Decision or consumer.** Harness author and user of a learned behavioral model.

**Alternative mechanisms.** If only a one-way observed session is available, preserve the session trace and do not pretend to answer arbitrary from-start queries.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Queries are interpreted as repeated experiments from one state, or a learner depends on revisitation of a modeled state.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** If only a one-way observed session is available, preserve the session trace and do not pretend to answer arbitrary from-start queries.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Reset outcome/hidden persistence specified; observation timing and label map stable; a no-reset result states connectivity/homing and counterexample assumptions.

**Environment and boundary.** Process, session, device, account and external-service state may have different lifecycles; a new socket need not reset all of them.

**Scope and exclusions.** Finite repeated observations support only those replays; they do not prove every future reset. Homing and reset use different premises and costs. Nondeterminism must not be inferred merely from forgotten state or timeout aggregation. Conversely, forcing a deterministic model does not explain true stochasticity.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** A reset/homing sequence may mutate real state. Legal/operational permission is an external premise, not granted by a learning theorem.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** **Claim links.** **Claim.** Strong connectivity and homing replace reset under a conditional probabilistic theorem.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0112

**Locator.** §2 and §4

**Claim.** Concrete protocol harness reset and timeout decisions.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0120

**Locator.** §3.1

**Claim.** Stochastic learner still requires step/reset interface.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0135

**Locator.** §3.4.1

**Specific requirement.** Inspect harness and persistent stores; use replay comparisons as bounded observations, not exhaustive hidden-state proof. Repeat authorized traces under stated timing and compare labels; model known stochasticity rather than discarding inconvenient outputs.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Canonical consequence.** A valid lifecycle contract complements BH03 but does not make approximate equivalence exact. BH07 separately assesses whether the effects needed for reset are authorized and restorable.

**Input conditions.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0202

**Original value.** C0204 supplies concrete experiment boundary; C0203 gives class-specific alternatives; C0214 prevents unknown oracle results becoming success.

**Input.** B:ESI-C0027

**Original value.** **Dependent or complementary property ids.** B:ESI-C0026; B:ESI-C0030

**Conflict.** Repetition can be expensive or irreversible; strong connectivity may fail at terminal states.

**Directional detail.** See criticism.json INTERNAL_RELATIONS; a listed complement is not an automatically established reverse implication.

**Failure of assumptions.** A stale login/session/counter survives reset, so identical words get incompatible labels misread as distinct states.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Fresh process startup, database cleanup, device reboot and trace retries can exceed learner CPU cost.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Invalidate replay evidence when reset mechanism, environment, timing or persistent storage changes.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0029; ESI-RCR0073

**Strongest objection.** Nondeterminism must not be inferred merely from forgotten state or timeout aggregation. Conversely, forcing a deterministic model does not explain true stochasticity.

**Known failures and misuses.** SOURCE-THEORETICAL BH003: without strong connectivity or reset, a run can enter a terminal component and lose access to earlier states. A stale login/session/counter survives reset, so identical words get incompatible labels misread as distinct states.

**Response or descendant form.** Homing and stochastic/nondeterministic learners offer alternatives, each with narrowed promises and extra assumptions.

**What changed and what did not.** A’s initial-state evidence and B’s lifecycle/replay treatment identify the same failure: nominally repeated words can start from different states. B separates lifecycle contract from observed replay consistency. Homing under strong connectivity and a counterexample teacher is a conditional substitute for reset, not free reset. A’s oracle correctness remains BH03.

**Residual limits.** If hidden server/account state is not observed or reset, classify the learner premise UNKNOWN or contradicted by an actual divergence; do not infer a reset from a reconnect command.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** If only a one-way observed session is available, preserve the session trace and do not pretend to answer arbitrary from-start queries. Actual mechanism: Bind each query to initial-state semantics or use an explicit no-reset/homing method. Detect contradictory replay answers and distinguish stochastic variation from instrumentation error.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0011; ESI-RTN0024

**Retention status.** CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

**Retention rationale.** Repeated words support a repeatable-state learning contract only when initial-state restoration or the specified state-revisitation mechanism and the observation mapping are justified. B:BH003 is the inspected 1989 Rivest–Schapire work; the later expanded version is not an independently read replication. A:C001 supplies Moore’s experiments distinction; B:BH011 supplies concrete TLS harness boundaries.

Apply the explicit outcome semantics below.

**Decidability and approximation.** Strong necessity of matching assumptions to claims; exact learning only under the theorem’s contract, not generic production completeness. The operational review is evidence-bounded; it must not claim a complete decision procedure beyond the selected model/theorem.

**Positive witness.** Constructed: a finite model oracle answers equality exactly and returns a replayable symmetric-difference string; theorem claim matches this access.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** Constructed: a random tester finds no failure in10,000 steps and the tool labels the hypothesis “equivalent”; exact identification is falsely asserted.

**Unknown conditions.** How to obtain sufficiently discriminating and affordable counterexamples for a particular live system. Also unknown when a load-bearing field is missing or assumptions cannot be checked.

**Inapplicability conditions.** A manually recorded trace is presented solely as that trace, with no generalized model or teacher guarantee.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** A deterministic test double can hide nondeterminism or durable-state leakage in deployment.

**False negative.** Demanding a reset when a proved homing/trace method suffices rejects a legitimate alternate regime.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Renaming an incomplete tester “exact” or silently excluding failed resets games the contract.

**Change invalidation rule.** Subject drift, durable-state leakage, changed abstraction, oracle strategy or budget reopens the contract.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Reset and counterexample searches may dominate cost; smaller discrimination structures reduce storage without making EQ free. Cheaper route: Passive characteristic data; direct property testing; homing/synchronization approach with its own assumptions; bounded model used only descriptively.

**Evidence ceiling.** Strong necessity of matching assumptions to claims; exact learning only under the theorem’s contract, not generic production completeness.

**Evaluation outcomes.** **Pass.** The precise scoped operational rule is satisfied with sufficient stated evidence; does not imply stronger truth, universality or adoption.

**Fail.** A valid witness or directly established mismatch contradicts that operational rule in its applicable context.

**Unknown.** The guard may apply but evidence, mapping, premise or computation is insufficient; this is neither pass nor logical negation.

**Inapplicable.** The declared guard is false; use the named non-trigger route rather than treating absence as failure.

**Evaluated proposition.** Claim-to-query-contract fidelity restricted to the initial-state/revisitation facet

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** **Canonical ceiling.** Finite repeated observations support only those replays; they do not prove every future reset. Homing and reset use different premises and costs. If hidden server/account state is not observed or reset, classify the learner premise UNKNOWN or contradicted by an actual divergence; do not infer a reset from a reconnect command.

**Source access comparison.** B:BH003 is the inspected 1989 Rivest–Schapire work; the later expanded version is not an independently read replication. A:C001 supplies Moore’s experiments distinction; B:BH011 supplies concrete TLS harness boundaries.

**Original ceilings.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0202

**Ceiling.** **Strongest supported claim.** Every learned-model guarantee must be tied to the actual observation/query contract and initial-state mechanism; exact equivalence may not be inferred from interface names.

**Unsupported stronger claims.** A tool named equivalence oracle is exact.; Every active-learning method universally requires physical reset.

**Limit.** Strong necessity of matching assumptions to claims; exact learning only under the theorem’s contract, not generic production completeness.

**Input.** B:ESI-C0027

**Ceiling.** Access-contract reasoning and bounded replay evidence; not universal reproducibility from finitely many successful trials.

**Transferability limits.** A reset-free finite strongly connected automaton result does not guarantee recovery of unreachable transient components.

**Unverified or open questions.** If hidden server/account state is not observed or reset, classify the learner premise UNKNOWN or contradicted by an actual divergence; do not infer a reset from a reconnect command.

**Next discriminator.** If hidden server/account state is not observed or reset, classify the learner premise UNKNOWN or contradicted by an actual divergence; do not infer a reset from a reconnect command.

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Symbolic/register learning and practical protocol mappers address finite-alphabet explosion and data-dependent memory.

**Original terminology.** Effective Boolean algebra, symbolic automaton, register automaton, mapper

**Original form.** Concrete values are too numerous for naive enumeration, while careless collapsing erases relevant distinctions.

**Original problem.** Concrete values are too numerous for naive enumeration, while careless collapsing erases relevant distinctions.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RGN0280

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Claim.** Symbolic learning is conditional on alphabet theory/partition learning.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0122

**Locator.** Definition1 and Theorems1–2

**Claim.** Register model and bounded comparative scalability; equality-specific query bound.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0133

**Locator.** §§6,8,9

**Claim.** Protocol mapper controls visible alphabet.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0120

**Locator.** §3.1

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** The candidate wording is a present synthesis. Named native terms retain their original scope; no claim that all branches descend from continuous control. Large-alphabet symbolic learning is not an automatic register-memory, timing or concurrency guarantee.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Choose a data abstraction and machine class that preserve the consumer’s material distinctions, while retaining the class-specific data theory, memory and query premises.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_ENGINEERING_MECHANISM

**Bearer or subject.** concrete behavior C, abstraction a, abstract model H, decision/property family Φ

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Concrete values are too numerous for naive enumeration, while careless collapsing erases relevant distinctions.

**Mechanism.** Distinguish predicates over a current symbolic input from comparisons against stored register values. A nonce can be fresh on one step and equal to a previously stored value later; collapsing those cases can erase required behavior.

**Mature or evolved form.** A’s richer-class rule and B’s data-class account both reject borrowing finite-alphabet guarantees after changing the represented semantics. A also covers time, nondeterminism and stochasticity, whose facets move to BH06. B contributes the explicit abstraction map, equality/order theory, register bound and finite-index conditions. Neither richer syntax nor a register tool proves all data-rich protocols learnable.

**Expected payoff.** Makes some data-rich systems learnable at useful size without silently changing the consumer’s question.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** BH013 proves theory-parametric symbolic learning; BH024 compares register learners with fewer queries on specified models. Live Mbed learning did not converge in the reported three-week run.

**Decision or consumer.** Engineer deciding which data, time and protocol features a model must preserve.

**Alternative mechanisms.** A small fixed finite alphabet with no relevant cross-message data dependence can use an ordinary Mealy model.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Concrete alphabets/state explosion or parameter relations threaten a decision-relevant distinction; the claim being evaluated specifies whether that distinction must be preserved.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A small fixed finite alphabet with no relevant cross-message data dependence can use an ordinary Mealy model.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** A declared abstraction map, guard theory/data operations, target model class and property being preserved; reliable concrete query realization.

**Environment and boundary.** A symbolic transition predicate classifies the current datum; a register can relate later inputs to stored earlier values. Neither supports arbitrary program semantics by default.

**Scope and exclusions.** Adequacy is relative to a declared observation relation and consumer. Equality/register results do not automatically extend to ordered domains, arbitrary arithmetic or unbounded memory. Preserve real-system feasibility limits: the 2026 SLλ Mbed attempt remained inconclusive after three weeks; the 24 intermediate-hypothesis experiments are model relearning, not completed live extraction.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Abstraction is an epistemic design choice, not permission to omit required distinctions or redefine acceptable behavior.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** **Claim links.** **Claim.** Symbolic learning is conditional on alphabet theory/partition learning.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0122

**Locator.** Definition1 and Theorems1–2

**Claim.** Register model and bounded comparative scalability; equality-specific query bound.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0133

**Locator.** §§6,8,9

**Claim.** Protocol mapper controls visible alphabet.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0120

**Locator.** §3.1

**Specific requirement.** Trace representative concrete witnesses through the mapper and compare relevant continuations. Read model/learner definitions and verify supported operations against the system slice.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Canonical consequence.** BH03’s abstraction theorem needs the target and fault domain after the same map. Root RT03 addresses general preservation, whereas this row retains the data-theory and memory conditions that give the behavioral claim content.

**Input conditions.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0203

**Original value.** C0202 observation contract is prerequisite; C0204 relates it to real experiments; C0214 prevents asymptotic or statistical claims becoming finite exactness.

**Input.** B:ESI-C0028

**Original value.** **Dependent or complementary property ids.** B:ESI-C0025; B:ESI-C0026; B:ESI-C0027; B:ESI-C0029; B:ESI-C0039

**Conflict.** State reduction can remove security/decision-relevant information; richer guard/data theories may destroy decidability or increase cost.

**Directional detail.** See criticism.json INTERNAL_RELATIONS; a listed complement is not an automatically established reverse implication.

**Failure of assumptions.** Two credentials/nonces or timeout ranges are merged even though their continuations differ for the consumer.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Mapper construction, symbolic solving, data-parameter exploration and counterexample minimization; register complexity may be exponential.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Invalidate when new values, comparison rules, message format or downstream property makes an erased distinction relevant.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0030; ESI-RCR0074

**Strongest objection.** Preserve real-system feasibility limits: the 2026 SLλ Mbed attempt remained inconclusive after three weeks; the 24 intermediate-hypothesis experiments are model relearning, not completed live extraction.

**Known failures and misuses.** EMPIRICAL LIMIT BH024: benchmark speedup on re-learning intermediate Mbed models is insufficient evidence that the full live implementation was identified. Two credentials/nonces or timeout ranges are merged even though their continuations differ for the consumer.

**Response or descendant form.** Richer classes retain selected relations and expose new assumptions; they do not eliminate the need to validate correspondence.

**What changed and what did not.** A’s richer-class rule and B’s data-class account both reject borrowing finite-alphabet guarantees after changing the represented semantics. A also covers time, nondeterminism and stochasticity, whose facets move to BH06. B contributes the explicit abstraction map, equality/order theory, register bound and finite-index conditions. Neither richer syntax nor a register tool proves all data-rich protocols learnable.

**Residual limits.** Find a fresh/equal/order counterexample and determine whether the proposed class represents it; obtain concrete query translation evidence before claiming an implemented learner for the live service.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A small fixed finite alphabet with no relevant cross-message data dependence can use an ordinary Mealy model. Actual mechanism: Define concrete-to-abstract labels and relevant continuation equivalence. Use symbolic guards for large domains and registers for remembered data equality/order when supported. Refine a mapping when a counterexample crosses an erased distinction.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0011; ESI-RTN0025

**Retention status.** ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE

**Retention rationale.** Choose a data abstraction and machine class that preserve the consumer’s material distinctions, while retaining the class-specific data theory, memory and query premises. A:C007’s undated longer Tomte author version and conference version have different reported experiments. B:BH013 symbolic automata concerns learnable Boolean-algebra labels; B:BH023/BH024 are versions of one SLλ research family, not two independent demonstrations.

**Source of the expression.** **Type.** RESEARCHER_OPERATIONALIZATION

**Rationale.** Operational rule derived from the source-supported limit/mechanism; not claimed as a verbatim theorem or universally mandatory process.

**Source ids.** ESI-RS0068; ESI-RS0069; ESI-RS0070; ESI-RS0082; ESI-RS0090; ESI-RS0091

**Observation or measurement map.** Distinguish predicates over a current symbolic input from comparisons against stored register values. A nonce can be fresh on one step and equal to a previously stored value later; collapsing those cases can erase required behavior.

**Required evidence.** Formal definition and mapping of a discriminating concrete example.; Audit teacher implementation and data-generation mechanism against selected theorem.; Trace representative concrete witnesses through the mapper and compare relevant continuations.; Read model/learner definitions and verify supported operations against the system slice.; Find a fresh/equal/order counterexample and determine whether the proposed class represents it; obtain concrete query translation evidence before claiming an implemented learner for the live service.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** First establish applicability. Inspect the two attributes and source witnesses; challenge the claim using the negative example; determine whether the stated supported condition, an actual breach, or unresolved evidence is present. Apply the explicit outcome semantics below.

**Decidability and approximation.** Specific conditional extensions and bounded benchmarks; no universal rich-system identification guarantee. The operational review is evidence-bounded; it must not claim a complete decision procedure beyond the selected model/theorem.

**Positive witness.** Constructed: a nonce-echo protocol needs equality with a fresh stored value; a register model keeps that distinction while a justified property ignores the literal nonce.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** Constructed: merging all timeouts into one label hides a deadline violation; applying a deterministic DFA theorem to that quotient does not repair the loss.

**Unknown conditions.** Which richer features are necessary for a particular property and affordable experiment? Also unknown when a load-bearing field is missing or assumptions cannot be checked.

**Inapplicability conditions.** A finite alphabet abstraction demonstrably preserves the only property being queried.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** A benchmark with visible resets can mask lack of reset visibility in the target.

**False negative.** Demanding internal-state identity when trace equivalence suffices can reject an adequate quotient.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Calling every unexplained output noise removes precisely the behavior the richer model should represent.

**Change invalidation rule.** Changed datatype theory, timing resolution, hidden state or probability law invalidates the class-specific result.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** More expressive classes cost solver computation, resets, samples and complexity; some algorithms become exponential or time out. Cheaper route: A smaller abstraction justified for the particular property, direct tests at selected data/time boundaries, or a deliberately incomplete model.

**Evidence ceiling.** Specific conditional extensions and bounded benchmarks; no universal rich-system identification guarantee.

**Evaluation outcomes.** **Pass.** The precise scoped operational rule is satisfied with sufficient stated evidence; does not imply stronger truth, universality or adoption.

**Fail.** A valid witness or directly established mismatch contradicts that operational rule in its applicable context.

**Unknown.** The guard may apply but evidence, mapping, premise or computation is insufficient; this is neither pass nor logical negation.

**Inapplicable.** The declared guard is false; use the named non-trigger route rather than treating absence as failure.

**Evaluated proposition.** Whether the data-class extension repairs a material loss without importing an alien guarantee

### Genealogy

**Original terminology.** register automata; residual finite-state automata; one-clock timed automata; deterministic labeled MDP; noisy MAT

**Original form.** Add data, time or nondeterminism while retaining useful learning guarantees.

**Original problem.** Finite alphabet abstraction can erase behavior relevant to the decision; “nondeterministic” names several different problems.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RBR0025; ESI-RBR0018

**Role.** Direct result/case or bounded complementary limit; consult source access level. Multiple references are not independent replications.

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not retroactively name every source Evolved System Identification or assert that all branches descend from control. Residual-language, register, timed and stochastic learning extend different parts of finite automata semantics.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Timed, nondeterministic and stochastic extensions require their own observation and equivalence contracts. Keep these as tagged alternatives; no single result supports all forms of behavioral variation.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_FORMAL_RESULTS

**Bearer or subject.** Target representation, concrete observation map and class-specific learner.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Finite alphabet abstraction can erase behavior relevant to the decision; “nondeterministic” names several different problems.

**Mechanism.** Record reset-time information for timed learning; separate unobserved output, quiescence and timeout for I/O conformance; identify sampling, confidence and convergence semantics for probabilities. Diagnose hidden state and scheduling separately.

**Mature or evolved form.** Both packets reject treating richer model names as an extension of an unchanged finite deterministic guarantee. A includes smart versus normal one-clock teachers, residual finite automata and almost-sure asymptotic MDP results. B adds table-relative partial-IOTS bounds, the completeness-oracle premise, race-avoiding timers and symbolic-only prototype limits, and fault-injected stochastic protocol models.

**Expected payoff.** Can represent distinctions a finite quotient loses; may reduce model size or interactions, at added access/computation cost.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Register normal-form result; timed teacher complexity contrast; residual automata succinctness; MDP asymptotic result and small noisy benchmarks. These are complementary, not independent proof of one universal method.

**Decision or consumer.** Engineer choosing a representation and admissible learning process.

**Alternative mechanisms.** A smaller abstraction justified for the particular property, direct tests at selected data/time boundaries, or a deliberately incomplete model.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Timing, timer races, multiple outputs, quiescence, scheduling or probabilities materially affect the modeled behavior or the claim made about it.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A finite alphabet abstraction demonstrably preserves the only property being queried.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Equality-only register guards, deterministic one-clock structure, residual-language equivalence, labeled-MDP observability or specified noise law as appropriate; never pool these premises.

**Environment and boundary.** A nondeterministic language recognizer is distinct from an interactive system with hidden branching; measurement noise is distinct from true stochastic behavior.

**Scope and exclusions.** Almost-sure convergence is asymptotic and is not finite-sample exactness. Nondeterministic languages are not hidden-process identification. Partial ioco bounds are relative to the tested table; zero observations do not establish zero probability. Preserve cost, oracle realizability, finite evidence and semantics mismatch. Do not merge stochastic noise, scheduling choice and unmodeled durable state merely because each yields variable observations.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Representational choice is analytical; no permission or intended requirement is supplied.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Concrete value/time/output traces, abstraction map, model class, teacher capabilities and any sampling/error assumptions.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Canonical consequence.** BH04 addresses lifecycle confounding. BH03’s oracle scope must match the chosen richer model. Root guarantee-typing cannot replace these native model restrictions.

**Input conditions.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0203

**Original value.** C0202 observation contract is prerequisite; C0204 relates it to real experiments; C0214 prevents asymptotic or statistical claims becoming finite exactness.

**Input.** B:ESI-C0029

**Original value.** **Dependent or complementary property ids.** B:ESI-C0026; B:ESI-C0027; B:ESI-C0028; B:ESI-C0030

**Conflict.** Long rare traces require many samples; race-avoidance can exclude exactly the concurrent behavior under investigation.

**Directional detail.** See criticism.json INTERNAL_RELATIONS; a listed complement is not an automatically established reverse implication.

**Failure of assumptions.** Wrong noise model can smooth away real branches; hidden resets can change tractability; data operations outside equality guards break the register abstraction.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** More expressive classes cost solver computation, resets, samples and complexity; some algorithms become exponential or time out.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-enter when unseen data operations, clock interactions, persistent branches or drift appear.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0030; ESI-RCR0075

**Strongest objection.** Preserve cost, oracle realizability, finite evidence and semantics mismatch. Do not merge stochastic noise, scheduling choice and unmodeled durable state merely because each yields variable observations.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: merging all timeouts into one label hides a deadline violation; applying a deterministic DFA theorem to that quotient does not repair the loss.

**Response or descendant form.** Narrow the target/property or strengthen observation access explicitly; retain the resulting cost and uncertainty.

**What changed and what did not.** Both packets reject treating richer model names as an extension of an unchanged finite deterministic guarantee. A includes smart versus normal one-clock teachers, residual finite automata and almost-sure asymptotic MDP results. B adds table-relative partial-IOTS bounds, the completeness-oracle premise, race-avoiding timers and symbolic-only prototype limits, and fault-injected stochastic protocol models.

**Residual limits.** Specify the actual variation mechanism and whether the learner’s required observations are implementable. When that cannot be established, keep the result conditional or UNKNOWN.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Listing richer formalism names without a discriminating behavior is unnecessary complexity.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0011; ESI-RTN0025

**Retention status.** ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE

**Retention rationale.** Timed, nondeterministic and stochastic extensions require their own observation and equivalence contracts. Keep these as tagged alternatives; no single result supports all forms of behavioral variation. A:C008 changes complexity with teacher reset information; A:C031 NL* identifies canonical residual language structure, not an internal nondeterministic mechanism. B:BH025 lacks a concrete tester; B:BH026 uses sampled protocol models with injected faults, not live MQTT/TCP/BLE deployments.

**Original form.** Reconstruct a tested implementation’s state behavior through an adapter and selected requests.

**Original problem.** The same messages can have different effects under different authentication, persistent state, configuration or concurrent clients.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RBR0019

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not retroactively name every source Evolved System Identification or assert that all branches descend from control. Software black-box checking and protocol state inference combine learned I/O models with controlled execution and independent interpretation.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Protocol observations and active experiments must be bound to the actual implementation, version, role, backend, credentials, concurrency, timing and allowed effects; generalized reuse may not silently enlarge that envelope.

**Claim class.** DOMAIN_ENGINEERING_CONDITION

**Bearer or subject.** A concrete protocol/API experiment and its resulting behavioral claim.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** The same messages can have different effects under different authentication, persistent state, configuration or concurrent clients.

**Mechanism.** Bind each claim to its concrete harness and state boundary, separately establish permission for the actual effects, and invalidate attribution after relevant context changes.

**Mature or evolved form.** Both versions require version/context binding and separate authorization for effectful queries. Agreement supports the inferential discipline, not a universal empirical benefit. A’s guard covers a generalized observation asserted or reused even in its original environment. B’s text emphasizes active exploration and cross-environment transfer; retain A’s wider assessment guard so passive but generalized claims cannot evade attribution review.

**Expected payoff.** Avoids claiming that one learned machine represents all protocol implementations and avoids invalid query semantics.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** TLS state-fuzzing cases demonstrate flaw-finding feasibility; ChatAFL demonstrates bounded test improvements. No universal experiment-authorization doctrine is claimed from these papers.

**Decision or consumer.** Protocol debugger, test author or security reviewer interpreting specific executions.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Read existing documentation, inspect a narrow source slice, replay authorized examples, or use passive observations when active effects are not permitted.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** An active stateful protocol experiment is performed, or a learned/generalized protocol observation is asserted or reused as evidence. Missing authorization/reset/version evidence does not switch the guard off.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** No active stateful protocol experiment is performed and no learned/generalized protocol observation is asserted or reused; only a supplied concrete message or example is described.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** The tested context and abstraction are recorded; initial-state meaning, asynchronous responses and persistent effects are accounted for.

**Environment and boundary.** Credentials, clients, timing, versions and durable side effects are part of the experiment boundary, even if outside the learner’s abstract state.

**Scope and exclusions.** The conclusion is about the named version/configuration/observation horizon. Historic implementation flaws and an old suite result do not characterize every current implementation of the protocol. Technical reachability is not permission. Reconnect need not restore account/backend state. A validated authorization boundary does not itself establish the state-reset or observation premise.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** A separate explicit authorization or applicable task scope permits concrete operations. Observed acceptance by the server is not permission.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Raw messages/timestamps, implementation/build/configuration, adapter version, credentials role, cleanup and replay outcome.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Canonical consequence.** BH04 supplies lifecycle evidence, BH03 supplies oracle semantics, and BH10 supplies authority for judging intended behavior. All three remain separate checks.

**Original value.** C0202 supplies oracle semantics; C0203 handles richer state; C0206 prohibits normative promotion; C0212 consumes independent property.

**Conflict.** The most discriminating action may be prohibited, irreversible or too costly; that reduces learnable scope rather than authorizing the action.

**Directional detail.** See criticism.json INTERNAL_RELATIONS; a listed complement is not an automatically established reverse implication.

**Failure of assumptions.** Different configuration or unrecovered state means cached membership can refer to a different subject; a replica may omit the critical production interaction.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Harness engineering, restoration, rate limits, interpretive work and replay can exceed learner computation.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-enter after configuration, authentication, durable-state or adapter changes; retire model when its consumer no longer uses it.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0031; ESI-RCR0076

**Strongest objection.** Technical reachability is not permission. Reconnect need not restore account/backend state. A validated authorization boundary does not itself establish the state-reset or observation premise.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: an authorized lab API fixture permits advance and read operations on a server-side counter. After advance changes the durable counter from zero to one, the adapter closes and reopens the socket and declares the modeled state reset to zero. A raw read after reconnect returns one, but the report attributes that response to the all-zero initial context. This demonstrated state/context misbinding is FAIL for C0204 even though every operation was authorized; it does not depend on a normative judgment about the API.

**Response or descendant form.** Use a smaller authorized experiment, passive trace analysis or explicit uncertainty; retain findings without pretending completeness.

**What changed and what did not.** Both versions require version/context binding and separate authorization for effectful queries. Agreement supports the inferential discipline, not a universal empirical benefit. A’s guard covers a generalized observation asserted or reused even in its original environment. B’s text emphasizes active exploration and cross-environment transfer; retain A’s wider assessment guard so passive but generalized claims cannot evade attribution review.

**Residual limits.** For an actual deployment obtain exact version/configuration, effect permissions, state restoration and observation mapping. No target was inspected and no live experiment is authorized by this research.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Do not require a universal protocol graph before answering a narrow API question.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0024; ESI-RTN0031

**Retention status.** STRONGLY_RETAINED

**Retention rationale.** Protocol observations and active experiments must be bound to the actual implementation, version, role, backend, credentials, concurrency, timing and allowed effects; generalized reuse may not silently enlarge that envelope. A:C011 was partial TLS access; B:BH011 reads the same work more fully, including nine implementations, harness details, Empty timeouts of 100–1500 ms and initial ClientHello outside the selected alphabet. This improves accessible qualification, not the study’s population or independence.

**Decidability and approximation.** Feasibility and bounded testing evidence for particular versions; not all implementations, safe production probing or universal security assurance. The operational review is evidence-bounded; it must not claim a complete decision procedure beyond the selected model/theorem.

**Positive witness.** Constructed: an authorized lab API fixture records its build, credential role and mapper. Its reset actually restores the modeled server counter to zero, as a raw read confirms. The report attributes the resulting response only to that recorded context. The protocol-boundary predicate is PASS.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** Constructed: an authorized lab API fixture permits advance and read operations on a server-side counter. After advance changes the durable counter from zero to one, the adapter closes and reopens the socket and declares the modeled state reset to zero. A raw read after reconnect returns one, but the report attributes that response to the all-zero initial context. This demonstrated state/context misbinding is FAIL for C0204 even though every operation was authorized; it does not depend on a normative judgment about the API.

**Unknown conditions.** A protocol experiment or generalized observation claim is present, but relevant implementation/state/credential binding, restoration evidence, observation-map meaning or effect authorization is missing or inconclusive. Absence of this evidence is UNKNOWN; a demonstrated wrong attribution or effect breach is FAIL.

**Inapplicability conditions.** No active stateful protocol experiment is performed and no learned/generalized protocol observation is asserted or reused; only a supplied concrete message or example is described.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** A test fixture can appear isolated while sharing persistent backend state.

**False negative.** Overly broad effect classification can block a harmless direct example already authorized.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Declaring the entire environment the model boundary without observing it provides no assurance.

**Change invalidation rule.** Build/config/credential/adapter/timeouts or concurrency changes re-open affected findings.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Harness engineering, restoration, rate limits, interpretive work and replay can exceed learner computation. Cheaper route: Read existing documentation, inspect a narrow source slice, replay authorized examples, or use passive observations when active effects are not permitted.

**Evidence ceiling.** Feasibility and bounded testing evidence for particular versions; not all implementations, safe production probing or universal security assurance.

**Evaluation outcomes.** **Pass.** The precise scoped operational rule is satisfied with sufficient stated evidence; does not imply stronger truth, universality or adoption.

**Fail.** A valid witness or directly established mismatch contradicts that operational rule in its applicable context.

**Unknown.** The guard may apply but evidence, mapping, premise or computation is insufficient; this is neither pass nor logical negation.

**Inapplicable.** The declared guard is false; use the named non-trigger route rather than treating absence as failure.

**Evaluated proposition.** Fidelity of a protocol observation/experiment to its version, state and effect envelope
