### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Recent LLM-based protocol, contract, architecture and interactive-learning work proposes richer automated reconstruction; evidence remains task-specific.

**Original terminology.** agentic automata learning; architecture recovery; formal specification synthesis; benchmark adequacy

**Original form.** An LLM agent can autonomously recover semantically adequate models/specifications across diverse unseen software environments.

**Original problem.** Plausible syntax, benchmark overlap and successful partial extraction can be mistaken for broad semantic fidelity.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RBR0024

**Influence or relation class.** Source-specific documented ancestry where cited; operational predicate and cross-domain constraint are present analytical reconstruction, not claimed historical wording.

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** ESI-RS0081

**Locators.** §1 motivation/open challenges; agenda sections on abstractions, oracles, noise and richer models

**Claim supported.** The 2026 research agenda identifies ongoing oracle, abstraction and richer-model challenges; it is not a new general impossibility theorem.

**Role.** Direct result/case or bounded complementary limit; consult source access level. Multiple references are not independent replications.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0083

**Locators.** §V pp.9–10, six implementations and protocol/model versions; Tables II–IV; coverage definition: unique response codes and union of observed states

**Claim supported.** ChatAFL reports bounded text-protocol fuzzing benefits; response-code coverage is a proxy rather than hidden-state ground truth.

**Role.** Direct result/case or bounded complementary limit; consult source access level. Multiple references are not independent replications.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0084

**Locators.** §III mutation/verification loop; §V-D15-program15-student blind rating; §VI-A50 isolated Defects4J files; §VI-B leakage/verifier threats

**Claim supported.** SpecGen reports verifiable-contract generation and a selected human-rating study; its real-file extension lacks reference specifications.

**Role.** Direct result/case or bounded complementary limit; consult source access level. Multiple references are not independent replications.

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not retroactively name every source Evolved System Identification or assert that all branches descend from control. Recent LLM-based protocol, contract, architecture and interactive-learning work proposes richer automated reconstruction; evidence remains task-specific.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Current bounded evaluations do not settle a broad claim that autonomous LLM systems reliably reconstruct unseen software semantics across distributions, versions and task classes.

**Claim class.** CONTESTED_FRONTIER_CAPABILITY

**Bearer or subject.** A stated LLM/scaffold/version applied to a defined reconstruction task and target distribution.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Plausible syntax, benchmark overlap and successful partial extraction can be mistaken for broad semantic fidelity.

**Mechanism.** Bind capability claims to model, scaffold, tools, tasks, run accounting and independent semantic checks; distinguish finite success, measured error and transfer to unseen populations.

**Mature or evolved form.** Retains A’s unresolved capability claim rather than merging it with B0041’s refutable exact-oracle universal or B0040’s positive grounding discipline. A includes recent autonomous automata-learning, Java-model extraction and code-comprehension studies. Their populations and outcomes differ from LLM-assisted proof acceptance or individual membership-label correctness.

**Expected payoff.** Potential reduction in manual specification/architecture work; not yet a general demonstrated effect.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** SpecGen/ChatAFL positive bounded results; ESEM17 systems extraction F1 and June 2026 exact-DFA benchmark expose failures; October 2026 Spec-Harness improves selected adequacy metrics, not all tasks.

**Decision or consumer.** Person choosing whether to rely on an autonomous reconstruction result.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Classical learner for finite DFA tasks; deterministic extraction; direct tests; LLM-assisted proposal followed by independent checks under C0213.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A result is trusted as generally semantically faithful because an LLM generated or explained it, or a broad autonomous reconstruction capability is asserted.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** An LLM writes an explicitly provisional label or candidate that is independently checked before use.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Versioned model/scaffold, available evidence, task distribution, budgets, groundtruth/reference quality and training-overlap risks are specified.

**Environment and boundary.** Benchmarks differ: exact language equality, endpoint/edge extraction, partition similarity and formal-contract tests are not interchangeable.

**Scope and exclusions.** General reliability across unseen tasks is not exactness on every query. Failure on existing benchmarks does not prove permanent impossibility; successful repeated runs on one application are not independent new applications. Preserve public-benchmark leakage, denominator, failed-run, scaffold and evaluator dependence. Current negative examples limit broad claims but do not license a timeless claim that future autonomous systems cannot improve.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Generated contracts receive no normative authority from model confidence or verifier success.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Task/input snapshots, prompts/tools/model version, all failed/partial outputs, evaluator version, comparator and train/test provenance.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Canonical consequence.** BH19 retains the stronger exact-oracle negative; BH21 assesses matched comparative benefit; BH22 assesses independently grounded outputs; BH23 evaluates reporting. Passing one does not settle this population-level capability claim.

**Input conditions.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0211

**Original value.** C0202 applies to LLM oracle use; C0207 to architecture; C0213 retains bounded utility; C0214 handles evaluator semantics.

**Failure of assumptions.** Changing public model/API or distribution, hidden reference dependence, prompt scaffolding or denied tools can change outcomes.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Long agent runs, API spend, validation and expert correction can exceed classical methods; report total cost including failures.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Capability claims expire with model/scaffold/task changes; re-enter on a specific improved method or meaningful external result.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0038

**Strongest objection.** Preserve public-benchmark leakage, denominator, failed-run, scaffold and evaluator dependence. Current negative examples limit broad claims but do not license a timeless claim that future autonomous systems cannot improve.

**Known failures and misuses.** Observed, version-specific: Menaged et al. v1 (15 June 2026) reports no tested model above 25% success at nine states in its 80-target/six-configuration benchmark. The current v2 (27 September 2026) instead tests 160 targets, three high-reasoning models and two scaffolds: best success for the 8–9-state bucket is 30.0% stateless and 57.5% stateful. Stateful improvements coexist with substantial failures and harm to Gemini 3.8 Flash. Liljas et al. separately reports incomplete architecture extraction. These are bounded observed failures and successor responses, not a claim that v1's percentage remains the current frontier.

**Response or descendant form.** Preserve tested task failures and specific utility simultaneously; assess a new bounded claim rather than extrapolating one global verdict.

**What changed and what did not.** Retains A’s unresolved capability claim rather than merging it with B0041’s refutable exact-oracle universal or B0040’s positive grounding discipline. A includes recent autonomous automata-learning, Java-model extraction and code-comprehension studies. Their populations and outcomes differ from LLM-assisted proof acceptance or individual membership-label correctness.

**Residual limits.** Require an independently specified unseen distribution, complete run denominators, semantic checks and fair model/scaffold comparison. No such general result is established here.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A multi agent label, fluent narrative or rendered diagram is no substitute for independently checked correspondence.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0016

**Retention status.** UNRESOLVED

**Retention rationale.** Current bounded evaluations do not settle a broad claim that autonomous LLM systems reliably reconstruct unseen software semantics across distributions, versions and task classes. A:C034 v1 and retitled v2 change tasks, models and scaffolds, so 80 versus 160 tasks is not a controlled longitudinal capability gain. A:C026 has 17 Java applications and 20 retained runs each, not 340 independent systems; A:C027 has six public systems and identity stripping, not a training-data contamination audit.

### Claim and mechanism

**Claim supported.** Learned TLS state behavior exposed flaws in particular implementations and required independent protocol interpretation.

**Role.** Direct result/case or bounded complementary limit; consult source access level. Multiple references are not independent replications.

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not retroactively name every source Evolved System Identification or assert that all branches descend from control. Peled, Vardi, Yannakakis 1999 explicitly combine active learning and model checking for black-box implementations.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** An independently defined property can guide black-box exploration toward a decisive violation before a complete model is learned, but a model-level counterexample becomes a system violation only with valid replay or equivalent system evidence.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_FORMAL_METHOD

**Bearer or subject.** Finite-state system, independent desired property, learned model and execution counterexample.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A complete model may be expensive and a model-level violation may be spurious.

**Mechanism.** Interleave hypothesized behavior, property checking and controlled replay; distinguish a real violating trace from a spurious model artifact. Satisfaction claims retain stronger finite-bound, reset, determinism, alphabet and observation premises.

**Mature or evolved form.** This A-only claim remains distinct from model ROI and LLM-grounding even where those rows cite later black-box-checking cost work. B:BH034 contributes later bounded query-cost context but is not property ancestry for B0042. The 1999 mechanism and replay bearer remain independently represented.

**Expected payoff.** Potentially finds a real property violation before full reconstruction.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Original algorithm and stated assumptions; protocol state-fuzzing provides related practical feasibility, not a replication of complete checker guarantees.

**Decision or consumer.** A checker deciding a specific desired property, not recovering all source architecture.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Direct hand-written property tests; bounded conformance; inspect source for the exact property.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** An independently defined property is to be checked against a black box, or a black-box property-checking conclusion is asserted. Missing access, reset or observation evidence is a premise failure/unknown, not a false guard.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Only descriptive exploration is sought: no desired checking property is supplied and no property-checking conclusion is claimed or relied on.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Deterministic finite target, known state bound for completeness, reliable reset, known alphabet and ability to observe enabled input/outputs as the original setting requires.

**Environment and boundary.** Positive no-bug termination differs from finding one replayed bad trace; without bound, budgeted search is not universal verification.

**Scope and exclusions.** A replayed finite bad trace can witness existential violation. Absence of a bad trace implies satisfaction only under a complete justified conditional analysis, not ordinary finite exploration. Desired behavior must be independent of the recovered model. A bad path in an overapproximation may be infeasible; a model with no bad path may omit the real violation.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Desired property must be independently supplied and scoped; the learner does not invent its authority.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Property version, experiment context, model/hypothesis version, candidate word, raw replay and refinement outcome.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Canonical consequence.** BH10 supplies normative basis for a desired requirement when needed, BH04 state validity, BH03 completeness semantics, and BH23 honest evaluator meaning. Their absence leaves the checking conclusion conditional or UNKNOWN.

**Input conditions.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0212

**Original value.** C0202 supports experiment theorem; C0204 bounds real execution; C0206 supplies authority distinction; C0214 separates unknown from pass.

**Failure of assumptions.** A hidden state beyond bound or unreliable reset can defeat completeness; replay mismatch can reveal abstraction/nondeterminism rather than a spurious logical path alone.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Testing and reset cost can dominate; stop when real counterexample answers negative question or budget ceiling reached.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-enter after property/system/adapter changes; a changed requirement can make previous finding irrelevant.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0039

**Strongest objection.** Desired behavior must be independent of the recovered model. A bad path in an overapproximation may be infeasible; a model with no bad path may omit the real violation.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: model-only bad trace fails on the actual system, yet tool reports a live defect without replay.

**Response or descendant form.** Use bounded bug-finding conclusions or narrower fixture while retaining the independent property and replay mechanism.

**What changed and what did not.** This A-only claim remains distinct from model ROI and LLM-grounding even where those rows cite later black-box-checking cost work. B:BH034 contributes later bounded query-cost context but is not property ancestry for B0042. The 1999 mechanism and replay bearer remain independently represented.

**Residual limits.** Obtain replay under the actual context for a violation claim, or the native complete-checking premises for satisfaction. No target system was queried in this reconciliation.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Complete behavioral reconstruction is not required before a real counterexample can decide a safety failure.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** A property weakened to match learned behavior makes checking trivially pass.

**Change invalidation rule.** Changed property, version, state bound or reset semantics reopens prior checking conclusions.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Testing and reset cost can dominate; stop when real counterexample answers negative question or budget ceiling reached. Cheaper route: Direct hand-written property tests; bounded conformance; inspect source for the exact property.

**Evidence ceiling.** Conditional checking theorem and replayed violation, not unrestricted blackbox certification.

**Fail.** A valid witness or directly established mismatch contradicts that operational rule in its applicable context.

**Unknown.** The guard may apply but evidence, mapping, premise or computation is insufficient; this is neither pass nor logical negation.

**Inapplicable.** The declared guard is false; use the named non-trigger route rather than treating absence as failure.

ChatAFL2024 and SpecGen 2025 use language models within conventional execution/verification loops;2026 Spec-Harness adds adequacy feedback.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A claimed benefit of LLM-assisted testing or specification must be supported on a matched task and outcome with a meaningful comparator and declared resource boundary.

**Claim class.** BOUNDED_EMPIRICAL_EFFECT

**Bearer or subject.** A specified assistance pipeline, comparator and measured task outcome.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Generating valid protocol sequences or expressive candidates by hand/template alone can be expensive.

**Mechanism.** Identify what the LLM proposes, what independently judges it, the baseline, complete task/run denominator and relevant time/query/review/compute costs. Evaluate the particular improvement claimed, not generic AI usefulness.

**Mature or evolved form.** Retains A’s comparative-benefit target independently of B0040’s per-output grounding target. Grounded candidates and legitimate adoption can form a usable scoped pipeline without establishing comparative utility. Correct A:REL-C013’s composition accordingly: add comparator/outcome/resource evidence before deriving this row.

**Expected payoff.** More useful test exploration or stronger candidate contracts in examined settings.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** ChatAFL reports comparisons on six text protocol implementations; SpecGen reports more verifiable Java cases and a selected rating study; Spec-Harness shows held-out adequacy gains with mixed statistical significance across agents/tasks.

**Decision or consumer.** Tester/developer deciding whether the assistance earns its cost for a particular task.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Use a classical learner/fuzzer, hand-selected example, direct assertion or static template when adequate. If such a route is an evidenced comparator that contradicts an asserted LLM advantage, the comparative claim is FAIL. If the comparison is not yet established, it is UNKNOWN. INAPPLICABLE requires absence of the comparative claim/use, not a cheap alternative.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A bounded comparative-benefit claim is asserted or relied on, whether or not the comparator, evaluator or cost evidence has already been collected.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** No comparative-benefit claim about LLM assistance is made or relied on. Merely choosing a classical method, or discovering that it is cheaper, does not make an asserted LLM-benefit claim inapplicable.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Versioned LLM/pipeline, fair budget, adequate outcome metric, clear failed attempt denominator and no automatic normative promotion.

**Environment and boundary.** Text protocol benchmark results do not transfer automatically to binary protocols; verifiability is not contract completeness.

**Scope and exclusions.** Comparison is within a named task population, model/scaffold version, outcome and budget. Equal-duration fuzzing coverage, successful specification proof and complete economic return are different estimands. A cheaper classical baseline contradicts a claimed cost advantage; it does not deactivate the assessment. Missing fair comparator yields UNKNOWN. Failed generations and validation labor belong in the relevant denominator/cost.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** LLM proposal is no authority; adopted tests/contracts still need their independent purpose and scope.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Prompts, models, generated candidates, feedback, all runs, budgets, reference version and actual executed/proved results.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Canonical consequence.** BH08, BH10, BH22 and BH23 can improve candidate/evidence discipline but do not entail benefit. Root RT04 supplies the general lifecycle comparison; this row preserves the actual LLM task and empirical populations.

**Input conditions.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0213

**Original value.** C0204 authorizes experiments; C0205 retains candidate status; C0214 evaluates adequacy; C0211 remains broad unresolved parent.

**Failure of assumptions.** A weak metric can reward invalid states, vacuous contracts or over fitted feedback; external API changes reduce reproducibility.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Include prompting/tokens, latency, solver execution, harness setup and rejected outputs, not only successful call counts.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Replace assistance when updated classical/cheap baseline matches value or pipeline change invalidates comparison.

**Cheaper alternative while applicable.** **Alternative.** An adequate classical method or direct example.

**Outcome when claim remains.** Its existence alone does not deactivate the predicate. A matched comparison contradicting the asserted LLM advantage is FAIL; unavailable comparison evidence is UNKNOWN. If no LLM comparative-benefit claim/use remains, INAPPLICABLE follows from that absence.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0040

**Strongest objection.** A cheaper classical baseline contradicts a claimed cost advantage; it does not deactivate the assessment. Missing fair comparator yields UNKNOWN. Failed generations and validation labor belong in the relevant denominator/cost.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: a pipeline claims lower total cost for producing the same required exact model, but a matched comparison establishes that the classical method produces that model at lower total cost than the LLM pipeline. The asserted cost advantage is FAIL, not INAPPLICABLE. A separate failure occurs when higher verifier-pass rate is obtained by deleting meaningful postconditions while claiming better specification adequacy.

**Response or descendant form.** Retain outcome-specific benefit, run comparable baselines and independent checks, report where gains are not significant.

**What changed and what did not.** Retains A’s comparative-benefit target independently of B0040’s per-output grounding target. Grounded candidates and legitimate adoption can form a usable scoped pipeline without establishing comparative utility. Correct A:REL-C013’s composition accordingly: add comparator/outcome/resource evidence before deriving this row.

**Residual limits.** Require a matched comparator and relevant total costs for the particular claim. No general productivity or cross-domain LLM advantage is established.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Multiple agents or complex prompt chains are optional; the mechanism is useful proposals plus decisive feedback.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0015; ESI-RTN0016

**Retention status.** DOMAIN_SPECIFIC

**Retention rationale.** A claimed benefit of LLM-assisted testing or specification must be supported on a matched task and outcome with a meaningful comparator and declared resource boundary. A:C023 ChatAFL studies six text protocols with ten 24-hour campaigns per condition and response-code proxies. A:C024 SpecGen has 50 isolated Defects4J files plus 15 programs from 15 students. A:C033 SpecHarness v3 uses held-out feedback and shared benchmarks; improvements are not uniformly significant or independently replicated by related corpora.

**Rule.** Each predicate decides its explicitly named proposition. Applicability, model truth, external warrant, retention and completion are separate axes. There is no default AND across alternatives or inherited variants.

**Positive witness or worked example.** **Reconciled target discriminator.** A proposed contract is independently valid but the same task is solved more cheaply by the classical baseline. BH22 grounding may PASS while a claimed cost advantage under BH21 FAILs; absence of comparator is UNKNOWN.

**Input witnesses.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0213

**Witness.** Constructed: a fixed task suite, outcome criterion and total resource budget are declared. An independent held-out check accepts more non-vacuous useful candidates from the assisted pipeline than from the relevant baseline, and all failed attempts and material costs remain in the comparison. A claim confined to that evidenced suite, metric and budget is PASS.

**Limit.** Input positive replacement examples do not constitute truth witnesses for a rejected universal. See each EVALUATED_PROPOSITION.

**Negative witness or counterexample.** **Reconciled discriminator.** A proposed contract is independently valid but the same task is solved more cheaply by the classical baseline. BH22 grounding may PASS while a claimed cost advantage under BH21 FAILs; absence of comparator is UNKNOWN.

**Input witnesses.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0213

**Witness.** Constructed: a pipeline claims lower total cost for producing the same required exact model, but a matched comparison establishes that the classical method produces that model at lower total cost than the LLM pipeline. The asserted cost advantage is FAIL, not INAPPLICABLE. A separate failure occurs when higher verifier-pass rate is obtained by deleting meaningful postconditions while claiming better specification adequacy.

**Non trigger example.** Constructed: an LLM supplies a provisional candidate for later checking, and no advantage over a comparator, task-value improvement or autonomous reliability is claimed or relied on. The comparative-benefit predicate C0213 is INAPPLICABLE; any separate candidate-validation obligation is unaffected.

**Observability and missingness.** Response-code states and branch coverage are proxies; held-out paired test outcomes measure narrower claim than full semantics.

**Currentness and invalidation.** New models, prompts, tool versions, protocol families or budgets require re-evaluation.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** **Canonical ceiling.** Comparison is within a named task population, model/scaffold version, outcome and budget. Equal-duration fuzzing coverage, successful specification proof and complete economic return are different estimands. Require a matched comparator and relevant total costs for the particular claim. No general productivity or cross-domain LLM advantage is established.

**Source access comparison.** A:C023 ChatAFL studies six text protocols with ten 24-hour campaigns per condition and response-code proxies. A:C024 SpecGen has 50 isolated Defects4J files plus 15 programs from 15 students. A:C033 SpecHarness v3 uses held-out feedback and shared benchmarks; improvements are not uniformly significant or independently replicated by related corpora.

**Original ceilings.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0213

**Ceiling.** **Strongest supported claim.** LLM components can improve specific testing or specification-generation outcomes when proposals are subjected to independent execution/semantic checks and costs are counted.

**Unsupported stronger claims.** Better coverage proves a complete correct model.; More verifiable contracts proves better requirements.

**Limit.** Local comparative effects, not all protocols/languages or intended behavior validity.

**Transferability limits.** Need new evidence for different protocol structure, code complexity, models and human workflow.

**Unverified or open questions.** Require a matched comparator and relevant total costs for the particular claim. No general productivity or cross-domain LLM advantage is established.

**Next discriminator.** Require a matched comparator and relevant total costs for the particular claim. No general productivity or cross-domain LLM advantage is established.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** An LLM may propose labels, abstractions, specifications or structural claims, but each output relied upon needs independent support appropriate to its particular semantic use and evidence boundary.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_ENGINEERING_MECHANISM

**Bearer or subject.** LLM output h, task t, reference/oracle o, evaluation E, use d

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** LLMs produce plausible labels/formulas/graphs whose correctness and generalization are not established by fluent presentation.

**Mechanism.** Record the model/prompt/tool role, grounding reference, contamination exposure, validation outcome and correction loop; distinguish proposal generation from judging, proving and adopting the proposal.

**Mature or evolved form.** Retains B’s per-output reliability discipline. Similar sources and controls in A0213 do not make it the same comparative-utility proposition. B spans L*LM, FormalBench, COINS, ATLAS and architecture generation, with distinct evaluators and reference artifacts. The contested status preserves unresolved grounding/transfer, not a claim that every output is false.

**Expected payoff.** May reduce hypothesis/abstraction effort or improve a specific downstream task while retaining falsifiability.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** BH028 shows demo/LLM combinations but membership errors; BH031 shows same-scenario agent-transfer gains; BH032 reports diagram judgments; BH029/030 expose semantic/prover limitations. No general reconstruction accuracy or lifecycle-saving result.

**Decision or consumer.** Researcher or engineer selecting an LLM-assistance stage and assessing its outputs.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Use an existing parser,known model,small example set or human explanation when that already answers the question.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** LLM output labels evidence, abstracts traces, generates a formal candidate or supplies a structural/behavioral claim relied on by a consumer.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Use an existing parser,known model,small example set or human explanation when that already answers the question.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Task,source evidence,oracle/reference,versions/prompt,baselines and evaluation population are explicit; unmeasured contamination/correction effort remain unknown.

**Environment and boundary.** External behavioral summaries are not evidence of an agent’s internal beliefs; same-task/environment transfer is not broad generalization.

**Scope and exclusions.** Support applies to each checked output or justified declared family. A validated finite label set does not make the generator universally correct, and same-environment held-out runs do not establish held-out-environment transfer. A self-judged candidate, plausible diagram or syntax-valid formula may preserve the wrong reference or omit a behavior. Shared benchmark families and reused mutations limit independence.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** LLM output has no independent normative force. Checker success establishes only its specified obligation under its trusted base.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0085

**Strongest objection.** A self-judged candidate, plausible diagram or syntax-valid formula may preserve the wrong reference or omit a behavior. Shared benchmark families and reused mutations limit independence.

**Known failures and misuses.** EMPIRICAL BH028: Tomita-language membership queries still contain incorrect labels; BH030 negative non-acceptance screening is not universal rejection proof. A fluent explanation or compilable formula is accepted despite a concrete counterexample or vacuous precondition.

**Response or descendant form.** Use explicit task/oracle roles,independent discriminators,negative examples and transparent unmeasured dimensions; evaluate concrete downstream changes.

**What changed and what did not.** Retains B’s per-output reliability discipline. Similar sources and controls in A0213 do not make it the same comparative-utility proposition. B spans L*LM, FormalBench, COINS, ATLAS and architecture generation, with distinct evaluators and reference artifacts. The contested status preserves unresolved grounding/transfer, not a claim that every output is false.

**Residual limits.** Obtain independent reference semantics and inspect all failed/unknown outputs. Ground-truth quality and public-data exposure may remain unresolved even when the tooling runs successfully.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Use an existing parser,known model,small example set or human explanation when that already answers the question. Actual mechanism: Ground proposals in traces/code/independent requirements; use deterministic checkers or proof assistants for the exact obligations they decide; measure errors and repair rather than treating generated output as an oracle.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0030

**Retention status.** CONTESTED

**Retention rationale.** An LLM may propose labels, abstractions, specifications or structural claims, but each output relied upon needs independent support appropriate to its particular semantic use and evidence boundary. FormalBench has 700 methods and 6,219 related variants, not 6,919 independent tasks. ATLAS uses 12 VMs with additional runs in the same environments and can harm the common path. ArchAgent compares against documents/author ratings; p=.00087 is not <.0001. COINS proof acceptance is under the stated trusted base and candidate screening.

COINS proof acceptance is under the stated trusted base and candidate screening.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Claims about tests, proofs, benchmarks and verifiers must preserve what their outcomes actually establish, including the proposition, assumptions, failed/unknown attempts and scope of aggregation.

**Claim class.** LOGICAL_EVALUATOR_SEMANTICS_WITH_EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT

**Bearer or subject.** An evaluation attempt, scoped proposition, evidence and aggregate metric.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Vacuous specifications can verify, true properties can fail proof, and benchmark denominators can hide missing/failed cases.

**Mechanism.** Map raw tool outcomes to communicated meaning explicitly. Distinguish proof of a formal proposition, a reliable counterexample, finite nonfalsification, timeout/unknown and vacuous satisfaction; preserve all attempt denominators and material code/contract changes.

**Mature or evolved form.** Retains A’s reporting/evidence-operation property as its own bearer rather than subsuming it into general guarantee typing. The underlying proposition may be UNKNOWN or false while the reporting-fidelity predicate PASSes. Root CL19 types guarantees; BH23 checks whether an evaluator’s actual records were faithfully translated into a claim.

**Expected payoff.** Avoids rewarding solver weakness, vacuity, altered programs or success-only statistics; improves meaning of validation.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Nimmer/Ernst observes true unverifiable invariants; Coins exposes proof-agent limits; Spec-Harnessv3 implements proved accept/reject, unknown checks and held-out feedback with bounded improvements.

**Decision or consumer.** Reviewer interpreting check results or deciding whether a candidate isfit for use.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Use a correct complete direct checker for a fully specified finite proposition when available. A faithful scoped report of that check is an applicable PASS; there is no requirement to manufacture an underlying UNKNOWN. More elaborate adequacy tests are needed only when the asserted meaning goes beyond the exact decided proposition.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A claim about what a tool, verifier, test or benchmark establishes is made or relied on. Missing evaluation evidence does not deactivate the assessment.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** No claim about an evaluation result's semantic meaning or acceptance force is made or relied on. A correctly executed exact finite check with a scoped result claim is applicable, not a non-trigger.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Evaluator semantics, proof/test budget, semantic model, reference provenance and denominator are known.

**Environment and boundary.** Logical outcome, benchmark credit, observational coverage and normative acceptance are different dimensions.

**Scope and exclusions.** Finite accepted/rejected examples and proof attempts retain their denominators. A proof is conditional on its model/assumptions; inability to prove is not falsity; checking a reference implementation is not automatically validating intent. Timeout-as-false, vacuity-as-adequacy, silently changed implementations, and deletion of failed attempts are material misreporting rather than mere confidence adjustments.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Acceptance policy may assign zero credit to unknown, but that does not make the underlying proposition false or grant normative force.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Original unmodified subject, exact obligation, premises, tool version, raw status/proof/counterexample, budget and metric aggregation rules.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Canonical consequence.** Complements all oracle/specification/LLM claims. An honestly stated UNKNOWN can PASS BH23 while the underlying adequacy claim remains UNKNOWN; passing reporting does not manufacture semantic evidence.

**Input conditions.** **Input.** A:ESI-C0214

**Original value.** SupportsC0202 oracle contract, C0205 candidate promotion, C0207 architecture evaluation, C0211 frontier claims andC0213 bounded utility.

**Failure of assumptions.** Unsound arithmetic, unjustified aliasing, model/code changes or incorrect test labels invalidate the logical interpretation.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Separate positive/negative proof checks and adequacy tests cost more; use them where a semantic claim depends on them.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-enter when evaluator semantics, program, contract, reference or aggregation changes.

**Cheaper alternative while applicable.** **Alternative.** A correct complete direct check of a specified finite proposition.

**Outcome when claim remains.** PASS when the communicated scoped meaning matches the documented exact result and assumptions. INAPPLICABLE is reserved for absence of any evaluation-result meaning/use.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0041

C0214 is FAIL because the communicated conclusion exceeds the evaluated evidence. The historical ESC/Java example separately grounds the warning that an unproved invariant can be true.

The underlying proposition may be UNKNOWN or false while the reporting-fidelity predicate PASSes. Root CL19 types guarantees; BH23 checks whether an evaluator’s actual records were faithfully translated into a claim.

**Residual limits.** When raw outcomes or semantic assumptions are unavailable, fidelity is UNKNOWN. The next discriminator is the exact proposition, raw attempt ledger, evaluator configuration and communication mapping.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A checklist of statuses without exact propositions, raw results or consumer policy is empty ceremony.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0015

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Reject a universal demand for an explicit state machine or formal diagram on every task. A particular artifact can be necessary for a named consumer or obligation, while a trace, table, example or direct measurement may suffice elsewhere.

**Claim class.** UNIVERSAL_ADOPTION_COUNTERCLAIM_UNDER_REVIEW

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** The presence of a diagram or explicit model is used as a proxy for a discharged behavioral or assurance obligation.

**Mechanism.** Compare the demanded artifact with the cheapest representation meeting the same concrete obligation. Separate local consumer requirements from a universal artifact mandate.

**Mature or evolved form.** Retains B’s ceremonial candidate independently of A0208’s architecture-graph necessity because the artifact, consumer interface and task population differ. The original predicate’s local necessity PASS can remain valid when named as a local justification assessment. It does not vindicate the universal requirement appearing in the candidate title.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Use the smallest representation or evidence that discharges the real consumer obligation; retain no extra artifact when none is needed.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** An artifact is demanded because it is called a model, state machine or formal diagram, or a claim of its local necessity is asserted.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Use the smallest representation or evidence that discharges the real consumer obligation; retain no extra artifact when none is needed.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** A legitimate local mandate would identify consumer,failure prevented and maintenance responsibility; formal assurance may genuinely require a model.

**Environment and boundary.** This rejects universal ceremony,not automata learning or required formal models in specific verification/control contexts.

**Scope and exclusions.** One adequate task without a new state-machine artifact defeats universal necessity. A model checker that specifically requires a machine can justify that local artifact without quantifying over every task. Keep useful explicit formalization and interoperability requirements. The target of criticism is an unsupported universal mandate, not the existence of a legitimate local artifact consumer.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** An authorized local process may require an artifact; research does not override it. A useful artifact still does not create normative authority for its contents.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Creation,review and synchronization burden without a material decision benefit.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Retire after its consumer/obligation disappears or a cheaper adequate representation replaces it; re-enter when a real state-dependent question arises.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0086

**Strongest objection.** Keep useful explicit formalization and interoperability requirements. The target of criticism is an unsupported universal mandate, not the existence of a legitimate local artifact consumer.

**Known failures and misuses.** CONSTRUCTED/source-grounded: a single replayed counterexample already answers whether a named behavior occurs; a full maintained state-machine diagram is unnecessary for that answer. A diagram is current and complete-looking but no consumer can say what decision it supports; tests or normative validation remain absent.

**Response or descendant form.** Retain the obligation and choose a representation with a concrete consumer and evidence-supported mechanism.

**What changed and what did not.** Retains B’s ceremonial candidate independently of A0208’s architecture-graph necessity because the artifact, consumer interface and task population differ. The original predicate’s local necessity PASS can remain valid when named as a local justification assessment. It does not vindicate the universal requirement appearing in the candidate title.

**Residual limits.** State the concrete consumer and obligation; if alternative adequacy or required interface is uncertain, local necessity remains UNKNOWN.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Use the smallest representation or evidence that discharges the real consumer obligation; retain no extra artifact when none is needed. Actual mechanism: The claimed artifact mandate has no universal mechanism; useful cases depend on a consumer needing state/trace reasoning,while some tasks need only a direct fact,witness or bounded rule.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0029; ESI-RTN0031

**Retention status.** CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY

**Retention rationale.** Reject a universal demand for an explicit state machine or formal diagram on every task. A particular artifact can be necessary for a named consumer or obligation, while a trace, table, example or direct measurement may suffice elsewhere. B:BH005 supplies task-bound reflexion practice, BH008 concerns targeted candidate assistance, BH019 object-centric representation choices, and BH021 situated accounts. These support bounded alternatives, not a proof that explicit machines never help.

**Original form.** Define theta~theta_prime by equality of induced observations or laws. g is identifiable exactly when it is constant on each relevant equivalence class; distinguish global, local, generic and point-specific claims.

**Original problem.** An optimizer returns a unique number even on a nonidentifiable ridge; priors/canonical conventions can hide rather than resolve ambiguity.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Ask whether the particular target g(theta), not necessarily every coordinate, is fixed across candidates indistinguishable under the experiment and observation model.

**Claim class.** MATHEMATICAL_MODEL_PROPERTY

**Bearer or subject.** A target functional g on an explicitly specified model class and observation/experiment family.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** XCL01: (a,b)=(1,2) and(2,1) give identical output for every u; more samples of this channel cannot separate them.

**Mechanism.** Define theta~theta_prime by equality of induced observations or laws. g is identifiable exactly when it is constant on each relevant equivalence class; distinguish global, local, generic and point-specific claims.

**Mature or evolved form.** Separate coordinate conventions from identifiable functionals; narrow or redesign the target/experiment.

**Expected payoff.** Prevents impossible parameter-recovery claims and identifies cheaper estimable combinations.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Constructed algebraic witness and inspected realization/definition passages; Bellman/Rothenberg original full proofs remain access gaps.

**Decision or consumer.** Interpreting fitted parameters mechanistically, selecting measurements, or transferring a model to unseen interventions.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Report an identifiable combination or an equivalence class. A task-specific decision can be certified without uniquely identifying the entire plant.

**Canonical common and distinct content.** Both assess whether the requested function is constant on the observational-equivalence class. A is more explicit about equality of observation laws, admissible experiments, local/global and exceptional-point scope; B supplies an equivalent operational condition and a distinct sum-only witness. Preserve these scopes, not a single rank slogan.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Interpreting fitted parameters mechanistically, selecting measurements, or transferring a model to unseen interventions.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Report an identifiable combination or an equivalence class. A task-specific decision can be certified without uniquely identifying the entire plant.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Model class, admissible inputs, initial-state treatment, noise distribution and target functional are specified; structural analysis does not assume finite data settle equality.

**Environment and boundary.** Inside the chosen model/experiment class; model misspecification can create false uniqueness.

**Scope and exclusions.** Exact equivalence-class statement in a specified mathematical class; no unqualified inference of unique generating mechanism.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** NOT_APPLICABLE as universal normative authority. This is a conditional scientific/methodological claim; any acceptance threshold is a separately stipulated consumer requirement.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Derive output map or likelihood law and exhibit invariances; solve symbolic equality or use qualified local tests. Source versions and access levels in sources.json; constructed witnesses explicitly tagged.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Choose feasible experiments to reduce uncertainty that matters to a stated decision, while accounting for experiment cost and operating constraints.

**Claim class.** QUALITATIVE_ASSESSMENT

**Bearer or subject.** A choice among admissible excitation/measurement designs, not merely a model-fitting algorithm.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** An input maximizes nominal Fisher information but violates actuator limits or excites an unmodeled resonance; Rohrs provides a related control consequence, not a direct optimal-design trial.

**Mechanism.** Define a design objective such as target variance, uncertainty-set diameter or expected decision loss; constrain delivered input, state/output, duration and reset options; test sensitivity to the nominal design model. In dual control the policy changes both the physical trajectory and future beliefs. Belief-state dynamic programming weighs those future observations by their effect on downstream expected loss. Klenske–Hennig §3.1 gives σ²_next = σ² Q/(u² σ²+Q), so the input changes posterior variance. Their §6.3 deliberately leaves an irrelevant parameter unexplored because it does not affect the required trajectory.

**Mature or evolved form.** Use robust/sequential design, bounded stopping and relevant finite-sample objectives when supported; preserve the passive-data alternative.

**Expected payoff.** Acquire more useful data per constrained experiment and avoid experiments whose information has no consumer.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Matched FRF example and exact-noiseless shortest-experiment theory support narrow payoffs; practical nonasymptotic2025 follow-up remains abstract-only. CL031 gives simple source-authored simulations, with 50 shared-seed runs per task, showing delayed and target-selective exploration. These are explanatory comparisons, not field safety or universal practical-value estimates.

**Decision or consumer.** New data can be actively acquired and the expected information benefit exceeds its disruption/cost.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Reuse passive operational data if they answer the target; use a short scalar probe or stop once alternatives no longer change the decision.

**Canonical common and distinct content.** Retain B decision-value optimization as a distinct claim from A external-action admissibility, which has a normative and safety bearer. Assessment of a proposed experiment must not require its benefit or authorization already to be established. Feasibility, authority and benefit are assessed premises.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** An experiment, data-acquisition design or its decision-value/feasibility claim is proposed, selected or relied on.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Reuse passive operational data if they answer the target; use a short scalar probe or stop once alternatives no longer change the decision.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** A feasible design set and resource limits are specified; predictive design model/noise assumptions are credible; closed-loop dependence accounted for. For CL031: declared initial Gaussian joint belief, observation/noise model, finite horizon and quadratic cost; static unknown parameters in the base derivation. Approximate Gaussian filtering, local quadratic cost expansion and numerical optimization are additional restrictions.

**Environment and boundary.** An optimum is relative to design/model/noise/objective class. No universal D-optimality, shortest-time or safest experiment.

**Scope and exclusions.** Conditional design comparisons and specific demonstrations; no general advantage for a named criterion.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** NOT_APPLICABLE as universal normative authority. This is a conditional scientific/methodological claim; any acceptance threshold is a separately stipulated consumer requirement.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Derive target sensitivity and forecast information under each candidate; verify constraints on the delivered experiment, not only commands. Source versions and access levels in sources.json; constructed witnesses explicitly tagged.

**Response or descendant form.** Use robust/sequential design, bounded stopping and relevant finite-sample objectives when supported; preserve the passive-data alternative. CL031 explicitly reworks Tse and colleagues’ 1973 approximation and extends it to modern regression features. It addresses the inadequacy of generic uncertainty bonuses by valuing only information useful to future control.

**What changed and what did not.** The retained or rejected inference is narrowed as follows: Use robust/sequential design, bounded stopping and relevant finite-sample objectives when supported; preserve the passive-data alternative. ### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Choose and estimate process and noise dynamics together with their assumptions; an easy least-squares fit is consistent only under the relevant regressor/error conditions.

**Claim class.** PROBABILISTIC_OR_STATISTICAL_CLAIM

**Bearer or subject.** A specified stochastic dynamic model and estimator.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Past-output regressors with colored equation error generally violate orthogonality; CL006 §8.1 derives the bias.

**Mechanism.** Use y=G(q,theta)u+H(q,theta)e, form innovations/prediction errors and minimize an explicit criterion. Polynomial special cases encode different shared poles and noise locations; Gaussian likelihood adds distribution/initial-state terms.

**Mature or evolved form.** Separate process and noise structures when warranted, use valid IV or closed-loop PEM alternatives, and evaluate on relevant independent evidence.

**Expected payoff.** Avoid systematic estimation bias and distinguish efficient special cases from unjustified simplifications.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Inspected algebraic bias relation and primary finite-time LDS bound under narrow assumptions; no universal superiority of PEM over IV.

**Decision or consumer.** Estimating dynamics from noisy input/output time series or interpreting LS/PEM/ML consistency claims.

**Alternative mechanisms.** For a known finite FIR with exogenous measured input and white output noise, ordinary linear least squares may be adequate.

**Canonical common and distinct content.** Both reject a universal least-squares recipe and bind the estimator to noise, model and information assumptions. A broader estimator account mentions IV, while B gives IV its own independently assessable moment condition. Preserve that mention as context and the separate CL06 mechanism; do not count the overlap as empirical corroboration.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** An instrument can repair regressor/error correlation only if it is sufficiently related to the regressors and orthogonal to the relevant disturbance.

**Claim class.** PROBABILISTIC_OR_STATISTICAL_CLAIM

**Bearer or subject.** Instrument sequence z, dynamic regression and error process.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Choosing z=u merely because it is measured fails if feedback makes u correlate with e; choosing independent irrelevant noise makes the cross moment rank deficient.

**Mechanism.** Replace LS normal equations by sum z_t(y_t−phi_t^T theta)=0; consistency needs zero instrument/error moment and nonsingular instrument/regressor cross moment, plus suitable convergence.

**Mature or evolved form.** Trace reference/noise paths, use filtered valid instruments and assess conditioning; choose another estimator when no credible instrument exists.

**Expected payoff.** Obtain consistent dynamics in some colored-noise settings without fully specifying the noise model.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Primary algebra and explicit thesis conditions support mechanism; no field effect size or universal efficiency superiority claimed.

**Decision or consumer.** Colored disturbances or feedback invalidate LS orthogonality while a valid reference/auxiliary signal is available.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Use ordinary LS when its moment conditions hold; no instrument is mandatory merely because data are a time series.

**Canonical common and distinct content.** IV exogeneity and relevance are a mechanism separate from generic estimator matching. Correct a guard that presupposes a valid instrument is available: assess whenever IV estimation or its consistency claim is used. Instrument validity is a premise to establish, not a precondition for asking.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** An instrumental-variable estimate or an IV-based consistency/identification claim is used or relied on.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Use ordinary LS when its moment conditions hold; no instrument is mandatory merely because data are a time series.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Instrument provenance independent of disturbances in the needed sense; correct process parameterization; rank and law-of-large-numbers conditions; closed-loop reference properties stated.

**Bearer or subject.** A state-space realization x_next=Ax+Bu,y=Cx+Du of specified external behavior.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A hidden mode with B2=C2=0 is absent from transfer data even if unstable; an identified minimal realization cannot certify the complete physical plant stable.

**Mechanism.** Markov parameters CA^kB factor through observability/reachability matrices. Rank exposes minimal externally represented order in exact conditions. InvertibleT changes(A,B,C) to(TAT^-1,TB,CT^-1) without changing behavior; subspace QR/SVD estimates these factors.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Model the actual feedback data-generation path before inferring plant dynamics; feedback creates dependence but does not prohibit identification.

**Claim class.** MATHEMATICAL_MODEL_PROPERTY

**Bearer or subject.** Plant/controller/reference/disturbance loop and estimator.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Treating u andv as independent because u was recorded, while u is generated fromy.

**Mechanism.** Trace u=r−Ky and disturbance entry; use a valid joint/noise predictor, known-controller indirect method, or reference-based instrument/projection as appropriate.

**Mature or evolved form.** Use method-specific direct/indirect/joint conditions; retain the identification/control interdependence.

**Expected payoff.** Avoid learning the controller or operating policy in place of plant dynamics.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Primary analytic limit and constructed static witness; no prevalence estimate of industrial misuse.

**Decision or consumer.** Controller or human operator changes inputs in response to outputs, including logged operational data.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Use simple open-loop LS only when the actual acquisition and error model meet its assumptions; no need to reconstruct an absent feedback loop.

**Canonical common and distinct content.** Both assess the dependence created by feedback and the need for informative reference/noise treatment. The constructions differ: A supplies an independent reference and recovers the true coefficient with IV; B exhibits an unexcited algebraic feedback ratio. Do not average these as performance estimates.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Controller or human operator changes inputs in response to outputs, including logged operational data.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Use simple open-loop LS only when the actual acquisition and error model meet its assumptions; no need to reconstruct an absent feedback loop.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Loop stability/well-posedness and controller/reference/noise assumptions required by method; relevant excitation and correct model class.

**Environment and boundary.** Correct direct PEM can be consistent; naive spectral or regression estimators may instead recover loop-induced relations.

**Scope and exclusions.** Conditional plant inference in a specified loop; not automatic causal interpretation of arbitrary logs.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** NOT_APPLICABLE as universal normative authority. This is a conditional scientific/methodological claim; any acceptance threshold is a separately stipulated consumer requirement.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Inspect equations/controller operation and reference provenance; derive population moments under feedback. Source versions and access levels in sources.json; constructed witnesses explicitly tagged.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Identification convergence, tracking fit or parameter boundedness does not by itself prove robustness or safety of the closed-loop adaptive system.

**Claim class.** ACCEPTANCE_OR_ASSURANCE_CONDITION

**Bearer or subject.** Plant, estimator, control law, unmodeled dynamics/disturbances and allowed excitation as a combined dynamical system.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Accepting adaptive deployment because nominal parameter convergence holds while omitted high-frequency poles interact with adaptation.

**Mechanism.** Analyze the closed-loop interconnection and uncertainty at relevant frequencies; restrict adaptation/excitation or use robust safeguards whose own assumptions are explicit.

**Mature or evolved form.** Preserve Rohrs negative results and Åström’s excitation/drift analysis; use bounded robust/adaptive configurations, monitor information and allow freezing. Dual control adds future learning to control planning, but preserves the separate burden of closed-loop robustness. A Bayes-optimal expected-cost policy may accept low-probability costly behavior; hard safety or worst-case robustness requires an additional property and corresponding premises.

**Expected payoff.** Prevent the estimator’s success metric from substituting for controller stability.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Serious source-authored negative simulations and analytical explanations, with contemporaneous critical response; not a reported field accident.

**Decision or consumer.** Estimated parameters or models change control actions online, especially when invoking nominal convergence proofs.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Keep a validated fixed robust controller and freeze adaptation when information is inadequate; adaptation is optional if it offers no supported decision gain.

**Canonical common and distinct content.** The shared bearer is a learning/controller system, not an isolated estimator. A supplies deterministic enclosure and safe-robotics premises; B supplies richer Rohrs body evidence and an explicit critical response. Preserve both without erasing disagreement over explanatory emphasis. ESI-CA-002 outer-boundary repair: the canonical property trigger is the union of its retained identification/control targets. B’s online-adaptation trigger cannot exclude A’s offline identified-uncertainty/fixed-controller composition; both child guards and their full schemas remain unchanged.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** An identified model or its uncertainty affects feedback actions, controller selection, stability or constraints, whether identification is offline or online. This includes online estimation/adaptation that changes control actions. Apply each retained predicate’s own guard and claim target: offline identification used to select or justify a fixed controller remains eligible for the identification/control composition assessment, without requiring online adaptation. A fixed controller is a permitted method choice, not by itself a non-trigger. Purely descriptive identification with no effect on control, safety or constraints remains outside this boundary; unresolved uncertainty or robustness premises affect the verdict within an applicable claim rather than excluding it.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Keep a validated fixed robust controller and freeze adaptation when information is inadequate; adaptation is optional if it offers no supported decision gain.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Specified plant class and uncertainty envelope; controller/estimator implementation; disturbances, saturation, delays and excitation bounds.

**Environment and boundary.** Rohrs targets studied continuous-time schemes and constructed examples; it is not evidence all adaptive control is unsafe.

**Scope and exclusions.** Conditional robustness of specified interconnections; neither nominal convergence nor case success proves deployment safety.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** NOT_APPLICABLE as universal normative authority. This is a conditional scientific/methodological claim; any acceptance threshold is a separately stipulated consumer requirement.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Derive interconnection and test/prove worst-case behavior under bounded uncertainty; keep adaptation and estimation claims distinct. Source versions and access levels in sources.json; constructed witnesses explicitly tagged.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Related property ids.** ESI-RC-RT01; ESI-RC-CL03; ESI-RC-CL10; ESI-RC-CL14; ESI-RC-CL16; ESI-RC-CL19

**Failure of assumptions.** No uncertainty envelope, unknown saturation/delay, or proof covers nominal plant only. Consequence: weaken or withhold the transferred claim, not automatically reject all model utility.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Robustification, monitoring and restricted excitation can reduce tracking speed or identification precision.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-enter analysis when unmodeled bandwidth, controller/adaptation gain, disturbance amplitude, saturation or model envelope changes.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0062

**Strongest objection.** Strong nominal proofs can be arbitrarily fragile to neglected dynamics; disputed explanations must not be collapsed into one retrospective story.

**Known failures and misuses.** Accepting adaptive deployment because nominal parameter convergence holds while omitted high-frequency poles interact with adaptation. CL031’s cautious one-step controller can reduce probing as uncertainty rises, causing the turn-off phenomenon. This is a source-defined failure of learning for that scalar model, not proof that all cautious or robust control is defective.

**Response or descendant form.** Preserve Rohrs negative results and Åström’s excitation/drift analysis; use bounded robust/adaptive configurations, monitor information and allow freezing.

**What changed and what did not.** The retained or rejected inference is narrowed as follows: Preserve Rohrs negative results and Åström’s excitation/drift analysis; use bounded robust/adaptive configurations, monitor information and allow freezing. The underlying constraint remains: Specified plant class and uncertainty envelope; controller/estimator implementation; disturbances, saturation, delays and excitation bounds.

**Residual limits.** Safeguards can trade performance for robustness and do not infer unknown high-frequency dynamics from low-frequency data. Approximate dual-control examples use simple simulated systems and an explicit model/prior. They do not supersede the Rohrs/Åström robustness dispute or certify an external adaptive loop.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Keep a validated fixed robust controller and freeze adaptation when information is inadequate; adaptation is optional if it offers no supported decision gain. Required mechanism is the bounded claim/evidence relation, not a universally mandatory artifact.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0019; ESI-RTN0022; ESI-RTN0023

**Retention status.** RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

**Retention rationale.** Identification convergence, tracking fit or parameter boundedness does not by itself prove robustness or safety of the closed-loop adaptive system. Safeguards can trade performance for robustness and do not infer unknown high-frequency dynamics from low-frequency data.

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Recursive identification predates modern online learning; exponential forgetting addresses change but can discard information in unexcited directions. Variable-direction and subspace tracking methods refine this tradeoff.

**Original terminology.** Recursive least squares; forgetting factor; covariance windup; variable-direction forgetting.

**Original form.** Exponentially weighted least squares discounts old errors; a recursion updates its information matrix. Direction-selective forgetting avoids erasing unrefreshed directions, but convergence still needs information and suitable drift/noise assumptions.

**Original problem.** Forgetting can create covariance windup and chase noise; remedies for boundedness can be mistaken for identification.

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not attribute this synthesized record wording to a historical author; Recursive identification predates modern online learning; exponential forgetting addresses change but can discard information in unexcited directions. Variable-direction and subspace tracking methods refine this tradeoff.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Online updating must track what information is being retained and lost; bounded parameters or frequent updates do not imply current true-parameter estimates.

**Claim class.** MATHEMATICAL_MODEL_PROPERTY

**Bearer or subject.** A recursive estimator, information matrix, observation stream and drift/excitation conditions.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Interpreting bounded coefficients under absentPE as proof that unknown dynamics have been learned.

**Mechanism.** Exponentially weighted least squares discounts old errors; a recursion updates its information matrix. Direction-selective forgetting avoids erasing unrefreshed directions, but convergence still needs information and suitable drift/noise assumptions.

**Mature or evolved form.** Use direction-sensitive updates or finite-window tracking with explicit error tubes; permit freezing rather than mandatory adaptation. CL035 extends currentness from drifting coefficients to drifting candidate weights, using distinct discount factors. This permits an old model to regain weight, but posterior updates alone do not verify a changed external regime.

**Expected payoff.** Adapt where beneficial while preserving information that new data do not replace.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Primary conditional results and constructed variance floor, not a field comparison of all forgetting schemes.

**Decision or consumer.** Plant changes enough to justify online adaptation and fresh data are informative about the changing directions.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Use no forgetting or freeze an adequate model when the plant is stationary or the current window carries no new information.

**Canonical common and distinct content.** Keep B recursive/forgetting mechanism distinct from currentness and the negative mandatory-refit claim. Refine applicability to an update/forgetting procedure or claim being used, without presupposing drift or fresh informative data.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A recursive estimate, forgetting/update procedure, or its accuracy/tracking/convergence claim is used or assessed.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Use no forgetting or freeze an adequate model when the plant is stationary or the current window carries no new information.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Specified forgetting/update rule; persistently adequate information for desired convergence or explicitly bounded tracking objective; numerical stability and noise effects.

**Environment and boundary.** Tracking a time-varying parameter differs from converging to a fixed true value; RLS covariance can be an algorithmic quantity rather than calibrated uncertainty.

**Scope and exclusions.** Specified estimator behavior and conditional tracking; no continuous automatic currentness guarantee.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** NOT_APPLICABLE as universal normative authority. This is a conditional scientific/methodological claim; any acceptance threshold is a separately stipulated consumer requirement.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Compute recursively from actual regressors; monitor directional eigenvalues and model residuals with defined numerical thresholds. Source versions and access levels in sources.json; constructed witnesses explicitly tagged.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Related property ids.** ESI-RC-CL03; ESI-RC-CL11; ESI-RC-CL14; ESI-RC-CL17; ESI-RC-CL18

**Profile id.** ESI-RPF043

**Profile dependence.** Weighted information spectrum and forgetting policy

**Tension ids.** ESI-RTN0022; ESI-RTN0023

**Failure of assumptions.** Unmeasured drift, undocumented forgetting, noisy regressors, or unavailable directional information. Consequence: weaken or withhold the transferred claim, not automatically reject all model utility.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** More forgetting improves responsiveness but increases variance and unexcited-direction vulnerability; monitoring adds effort.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Stop/reinitialize or change adaptation when information collapses, abrupt structure changes, noise bound fails or decision value disappears.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0065

**Strongest objection.** Forgetting can create covariance windup and chase noise; remedies for boundedness can be mistaken for identification.

**Known failures and misuses.** Interpreting bounded coefficients under absentPE as proof that unknown dynamics have been learned.

**Response or descendant form.** Use direction-sensitive updates or finite-window tracking with explicit error tubes; permit freezing rather than mandatory adaptation.

**What changed and what did not.** The retained or rejected inference is narrowed as follows: Use direction-sensitive updates or finite-window tracking with explicit error tubes; permit freezing rather than mandatory adaptation.
