### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Online estimation enables adaptation; variable-direction forgetting and current benchmarks expose why update frequency is not itself a payoff.

**Original terminology.** Continuous refitting; exponential forgetting; update benefit; lifecycle comparator

**Original form.** Automatically refresh model parameters whenever new data arrive.

**Original problem.** Routine updates can amplify noise, forget informative directions, spend resources or destabilize use without improving the decision.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RBR0014

**Influence or relation class.** CRITICAL_RESPONSE; REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** ESI-RS0052

**Locator.** Information recursion and introduction

**Specific claim.** Loss of excitation makes forgetting hazardous.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0059

**Locator.** §VI

**Specific claim.** Current online method still has noise, slow-drift and field-validation limits.

**Source id.** ESI-RS0058

**Locator.** §§4–5

**Specific claim.** Cheap baselines can remain competitive and some more complex fits are unstable.

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** The rejected universal practice is not imputed to every adaptive-estimation author. No claim that fixed models are always better.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Candidate universal proposition: updating continuously always improves model use. Reject it; require a material change/benefit case and compare against retaining the validated model or a cheaper fallback.

**Claim class.** UNIVERSAL_PRACTICE_ADMITTED_FOR_FALSIFICATION

**Bearer or subject.** A model update policy and its downstream decision/lifecycle cost

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Fresh parameters or lower training loss are substituted for improved useful behavior.

**Mechanism.** Actual useful adaptation responds to identifiable change with informative evidence; assess update error/cost against a fixed or simpler comparator before relying on it.

**Mature or evolved form.** Triggered, information-aware updates with retained baseline, validated improvement and retirement/fallback conditions.

**Expected payoff.** Avoid needless computation and noise-driven degradation while preserving adaptation when it demonstrably helps.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Recent nonlinear baselines and FEM/PINN timing studies show why training, evaluation and method-specific costs must be compared; neither supplies a universal ranking of refitting policies. The constant-target risk calculation refutes an unrestricted always-better claim; RLS information recursion provides a separate direction-specific failure mechanism.

**Decision or consumer.** Update now, retain the current model, gather data or fall back.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Fixed validated model; Event-triggered update; Selective forgetting; Direct measurement; Lookup/rule; Scheduled bounded recalibration

**Canonical common and distinct content.** A tests the always-better proposition; B tests removal/rejection warrant and qualified update alternatives. Keep both targets and separate currentness, change detection, recursive mechanism and value. ESI-CA-001 operative repair: bind the original universal domain and claim parameters, require whole-target proof for a universal PASS, and allocate real-drift benefit only to its separately bounded target. Solely bounded claims are INAPPLICABLE to the universal evaluator; unknown premises of an asserted universal remain UNKNOWN unless a reliable in-domain falsifier decides FAIL.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A policy claims continuous updating is intrinsically beneficial regardless of drift, excitation, cost or decision.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A constant known target with a validated exact fixed estimate needs no noisy refit; a stable bounded use can retain that estimate. This cheaper alternative can falsify the asserted universal when admitted by its original domain. The universal evaluator is INAPPLICABLE only if no criticized universal is asserted; a solely bounded update claim has a separate target.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Any positive update-value claim requires a defined decision loss, currentness/information evidence, comparator, update cost and reuse horizon; different cost dimensions are not summed without an explicit conversion.

**Environment and boundary.** Total decision value of an update over a stated horizon, separate from in-sample estimator fit.

**Scope and exclusions.** No universal rejection of online adaptation; no arbitrary numerical utility from ordinal model scores or incomparable timing/currency units.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Record old/new models, training and assessment data, detector/update policy, all tuning/validation costs and actual downstream use.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** C0110 currentness, C0111 honest comparison, C0101 regime and C0112 conditional guarantees. Frequent adaptation can conflict with stability and independence of evaluation.

**Failure of assumptions.** No drift, no excitation, noisy observation or biased evaluation can make the new model worse; expensive training can erase inference savings.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Retain the validated fixed estimate until informative change warrants updating; use selective/event-triggered methods when justified

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Update when new justified change/information can alter the consumer’s decision; retire the policy when measured benefit no longer covers its declared costs.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0022; ESI-RCR0027

**Strongest objection.** A fixed model can also become dangerously stale; rejecting universal refitting must not become a universal freeze rule.

**Known failures and misuses.** Executed constant-target example: validated fixed estimate 0 has expected squared error 0; refitting to one independent mean-zero variance-one observation yields expected error 1. Uniform forgetting adds a distinct information-loss counter.

**Response or descendant form.** Use targeted currentness checks, excitation-aware adaptation and independent comparator evaluation; retain a fallback when evidence is weak.

**What changed and what did not.** Adaptation becomes a conditional intervention on the model, justified by use value and information rather than cadence.

**Residual limits.** Real-world update cost/benefit and optimal trigger design remain context-dependent; no broad empirical causal benefit is established for the proposed recording policy.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Continuous refitting as a mandatory ritual is not a general engineering property; triggered informative adaptation is a mechanism.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0008; ESI-RTN0010

**Retention status.** CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY

**Retention rationale.** The universal practice has an exact counterexample and clear costs. Conditional adaptation is retained without making it mandatory.

**False positive and false negative risks.** Removing updates can leave a changing plant untracked; keeping them can create noise-driven churn and apparent freshness. A model PASS without external premise support is a false promotion; an overly broad guard can reject the legitimate cheap path: Freeze the adequate model, monitor relevant changes and refresh on material evidence; use batch sufficient statistics when appropriate.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Selecting the target/envelope after seeing results, omitting material alternatives, or reporting the convenient model result while suppressing unknown consumer, drift, update effect or cost; absent evidence cannot be turned into universal uselessness.

**Change invalidation rule.** Retire automatic updates when marginal benefit disappears; re-enter when material drift plus useful observations and safe update conditions are established.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Compute, validation, operational churn and possible noise amplification; removal saves these but can miss real drift without monitoring. Freeze the adequate model, monitor relevant changes and refresh on material evidence; use batch sufficient statistics when appropriate.

**Evidence ceiling.** Refutation of universal necessity plus conditional alternatives; no organization-specific cost savings claimed.

**Evaluation outcomes.** **Pass.** **Model.** The contextual construction defeats necessity of constant refitting.

**External.** A comparable operational baseline demonstrates sufficient decision value without mandatory refresh; no such field experiment was run here.

**Fail.** **Model.** The supposed cheaper baseline fails the same need or the comparison omits material drift.

**External.** Observed decision loss from stale model defeats the local removal proposal; it does not justify universal continuous refitting.

**Unknown.** **Model.** Unknown consumer, drift, update effect or cost; absent evidence cannot be turned into universal uselessness. The predicate is not thereby false.

**External.** Unestablished observation, class or premise correspondence: Unknown consumer, drift, update effect or cost; absent evidence cannot be turned into universal uselessness.

**Inapplicable.** **Model.** There is no imposed update practice, or a specific supported tracking requirement already governs updates.

**External.** There is no imposed update practice, or a specific supported tracking requirement already governs updates. Do not count inapplicability as positive evidence.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Validate the chosen behavioral class on the intended regime, horizon and observation protocol. Additional complexity requires a justified advantage over an adequate-access comparator under the predeclared consumer decision policy, subject to the applicable feasibility, risk and lifecycle-burden limits. Remedying consequential baseline inadequacy is one possible justification; a decision-relevant net benefit can also justify escalation when both models meet their hard tolerances.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_ENGINEERING_CLAIM

**Bearer or subject.** A nonlinear input/output model and its claimed operating envelope

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Good fit near one operating point is mistaken for adequacy at saturation, under another excitation type, or during unobserved mode transitions.

**Mechanism.** Validate representation adequacy for the declared consumer, then compare the actual candidate and simple alternatives under the predeclared decision policy. Use informative matched evidence, explicit lifecycle burden and separate hard constraints. A pure satisficing policy can retain an adequate cheaper baseline; a policy valuing further consequential improvement can prefer a feasible candidate with warranted net benefit.

**Mature or evolved form.** Validate the chosen behavioral class on the intended regime, horizon and observation protocol. Additional complexity requires a justified advantage over an adequate-access comparator under the predeclared consumer decision policy, subject to the applicable feasibility, risk and lifecycle-burden limits. Remedying consequential baseline inadequacy is one possible justification; a decision-relevant net benefit can also justify escalation when both models meet their hard tolerances.

**Expected payoff.** Detect model inadequacy before a prediction or simulation decision depends on an untested regime.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** The 2026 benchmark reports method- and dataset-specific free-run outcomes, including unstable PNARX on ParWH; it does not establish a universally best nonlinear method. Original validation work derives tests under analytic/input-moment assumptions; the proposed envelope predicate is not a theorem.

**Decision or consumer.** Whether to use a linear, block, NARMAX, state-space or switched model for a specified prediction/simulation consumer.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Linear approximation on a bounded envelope; Simple block model; Separate local models with explicit switching; Direct measurement or lookup table

**Reconciled mechanism and target distinctions.** A evaluates bounded per-regime adequacy. B evaluates whether escalation from a baseline earns its cost. Adequacy and incremental justification are different predicates, both retained.

**Reconciled shared content.** Purpose, regime, observation access and cheap alternatives determine adequacy; model size is not evidence.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Input amplitude/type, saturation, hysteresis or internal feedback materially changes the outcome relevant to use.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A small-signal linear model validated inside |u|≤0.5 need not be replaced merely because the physical device saturates outside the authorized envelope.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** A: finite per-regime error vector and tolerance, with unstable runs explicit. B: matched baseline access, consequential improvement, cost/risk limits. A model may pass adequacy while escalation remains inapplicable or unjustified.

**Environment and boundary.** Observed input/output behavior and specified envelope; internal mechanisms may remain nonunique.

**Scope and exclusions.** A: finite per-regime error vector and tolerance, with unstable runs explicit. B: matched baseline access, consequential improvement, cost/risk limits. A model may pass adequacy while escalation remains inapplicable or unjustified.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Record excitation design, sensor calibration, preprocessing fit only on training data, initial-state treatment and test regime labels.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** Depends on observation correspondence, informative excitation and C0111 validation; complex structures can conflict with C0115 cost and update stability.

**Failure of assumptions.** Unvisited regimes remain unknown; correlated/noise-driven apparent nonlinearity can lead to wrong structure choice.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Start with a linear/simple-block baseline; collect targeted regimes only when the decision needs them

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Revalidate when excitation distribution, sensor nonlinearity, switching logic or consumer horizon changes; retire the unsupported part of the envelope.

**Reconciled composition consequence.** FR02 noise placement, FR03 mode evidence, CL18 validation and RT04 value constrain the same decision through different premises; none is implied by a local fit.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0013

**Strongest objection.** A more expressive nonlinear model can overfit, simulate unstably and remain observationally nonunique; linear residual acceptance is not enough.

**Known failures and misuses.** The same unchanged model has absolute error 1 at u=2. The changed premise is the operating envelope, not the serialized model.

**Response or descendant form.** Use structured simple models, appropriate nonlinear diagnostics and targeted validation before increasing complexity.

**What changed and what did not.** A evaluates bounded per-regime adequacy. B evaluates whether escalation from a baseline earns its cost. Adequacy and incremental justification are different predicates, both retained.

**Residual limits.** Rare-regime loss and total benefit remain use-specific. Compare the actual cheap model and candidate at the receiving horizon with declared observation access.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A nonlinear label or mandatory global model is ceremony when a bounded linear model already supports the consumer.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0006; ESI-RTN0009

**Retention status.** RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

**Retention rationale.** Purpose, regime, observation access and cheap alternatives determine adequacy; model size is not evidence. A evaluates bounded per-regime adequacy. B evaluates whether escalation from a baseline earns its cost. Adequacy and incremental justification are different predicates, both retained.

**Name and plain language claim.** Nonlinear representation complexity is justified by its declared use and operating regime — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.

**Predicate kind.** ACCEPTANCE_OR_ASSURANCE_CONDITION

**Subject and argument signature.** JustifiedNonlinearity(candidate, baseline, use_contract, validation, cost_estimate)

**Variable domains and units.** Mixed categorical, time, physical-unit and currency fields; thresholds belong to the consumer. Attribute ESI-RAT0119 supplies the structured arguments.

**Quantifiers and scope.** Only the declared model, input/observation regime, horizon and claim scope. No extrapolation from local prediction to global simulation or mechanistic truth.

**State trace event or model bearer.** A model-selection decision and its use envelope

**Temporal and modal semantics.** Epistemic acceptance at the specified version; it is not a temporal safety invariant unless a cited theorem explicitly says so. Evidence remains valid only within its stated horizon and assumptions.

**Assumptions.** The consumer decision policy, hard feasibility/tolerance conditions, risk and lifecycle-burden limits, intended output, horizon and operating range are stated before comparison. Candidate and comparator have matched observation access and are assessed for the same declared use; comparison need not claim global optimality over unexamined alternatives.

**Applicability guard.** A nonlinear candidate is proposed for prediction, free simulation, control, diagnosis or explanation.

**Expression or precise operational rule.** Within a fixed use envelope and matched observation access, establish candidate feasibility and adherence to the declared risk/burden limits. Then determine whether the predeclared consumer policy warrants replacing the comparator. A consequential baseline tolerance failure remedied by the candidate can establish the feasibility route. When both are feasible, a warranted policy-relevant improvement after lifecycle burden can establish a net-benefit route. Under pure satisficing followed by minimum burden, an adequate cheaper baseline remains preferred. A merely smaller fit statistic, an unranked tradeoff or an invented cost exchange rate does not establish justification.

**Source of the expression.** RESEARCHER_RECONSTRUCTION of a guarded evaluation rule from the cited sources; not represented as a source-authored formula. Exact source theorem/identity terms, when used, are identified by source and locator.

**Observation or measurement map.** Bind the use contract, decision policy and actual candidate/comparator access. Use evidence appropriate to the claim: matched held-out trajectories for the stated empirical comparison, or an explicitly stipulated finite population/valid derivation for a mathematical construction. Account separately for lifecycle burden, risk, coverage and uncertainty; a constructed comparison does not establish external plant performance.

**Required evidence.** Record {decision including predeclared preference/feasibility policy and tie rule, predicted quantities and units, horizon, admissible inputs/states, measured-output access, hard tolerances, cheap comparator, lifecycle costs, risk/burden limits and their evidence/uncertainty}. Supporting source links are property-level context; a deployed judgment requires its own target evidence.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** **Steps.** Identify whether this is a nonlinear escalation/model-selection justification claim; if absent, use INAPPLICABLE.; Bind actual versions, same-use/access correspondence, predeclared policy, hard constraints and evidence classes. Do not create a preference or silently monetize hard constraints.; If a decisive known premise refutes this scoped justification (unmatched comparison, infeasible candidate, inadmissible risk/burden or a policy that rejects the candidate), return FAIL with that reason. This does not prove every differently scoped candidate claim false.; Otherwise distinguish the feasibility-remediation route from the feasible-options comparative-benefit route; account for relevant uncertainty and cheaper alternatives. Give PASS only if sufficient evidence establishes a permitted justification under the declared policy; missing decisive evidence or an unresolved tradeoff remains UNKNOWN.; Return the outcome, decisive evidence, declared scope and remaining uncertainty. Do not convert a mathematical construction into an observed external benefit.

**Outcomes.** **Pass.** Matched evidence establishes that the candidate meets applicable hard constraints and risk/burden limits and is justified over the comparator by the predeclared policy. This can be remediation of consequential baseline inadequacy or a warranted net benefit when both are adequate; hard-tolerance failure is not necessary for the latter route.

**Fail.** A decisive known condition defeats this scoped justification: task/access is not matched as claimed, candidate feasibility or risk/burden limits fail, or the declared comparison policy does not justify the added complexity. This includes a cost-dominated/no-consequential-gain choice or an adequate cheaper baseline preferred by pure satisficing.

**Unknown.** No decisive known refutation applies, but the decision policy, matched comparator, regime coverage, costs, risks or other decisive evidence is missing/unknown, or uncertainty/incomparable tradeoffs prevent the declared policy from deciding the justification.

**Inapplicable.** No nonlinear escalation or model-selection justification decision is under consideration.

**Decidability and approximation.** A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.

**Positive witness.** Constructed, fixed-contract example: for x uniform on {-1,0,1} and y=x², the best affine predictor2/3 has expected loss9 under loss(81/2)(prediction−y)²; the quadratic has loss0 and incremental lifecycle burden2. Both meet hard tolerance10, burden2 meets allowance3, and equal admissible risks are stipulated. A policy minimizing loss plus commensurate burden prefers totals2 over9. The same data under pure satisficing then minimum burden prefer the adequate baseline. These are mathematical controls, not an external cost-effectiveness trial; mixed published benchmarks retain their separate limited support.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** Constructed: one-step prediction with frequent measured-output resets looks excellent, but the consumer needs a long free rollout that diverges.

**Unknown conditions.** No decisive known refutation applies, but the decision policy, matched comparator, regime coverage, costs, risks or other decisive evidence is missing/unknown, or uncertainty/incomparable tradeoffs prevent the declared policy from deciding the justification.

**Inapplicability conditions.** No nonlinear escalation or model-selection justification decision is under consideration.

**False positive and false negative risks.** False positive: expressiveness, a smaller fit statistic, mismatched access, speculative reuse or undeclared exchange rates are mistaken for decision benefit. False negative: hard-tolerance satisfaction alone is used to prohibit a demonstrated net-beneficial choice under a policy valuing that improvement, or local adequacy hides relevant untested regimes. Neither error justifies universal nonlinear escalation.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. Nonlinear models are universally superior.

**Change invalidation rule.** Reassess after regime, controller, horizon or consequence changes; retire complexity whose incremental benefit disappears.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Count experiment, fitting, validation, deployment, monitoring, maintenance and downstream burden over the stated horizon. A stable local linear/lookup model can remain the justified choice when its adequacy and the declared policy give no warranted advantage to added complexity. Adequacy alone does not prove that no policy-relevant net benefit exists.

**Evidence ceiling.** No extrapolation from local prediction to global simulation or mechanistic truth. Choosing the consequence function and obtaining rare-regime data remain judgment-dependent. The 2019 roadmap supplies methodological rationale; the 2026 baseline paper supplies mixed family rankings. Neither is a universal cost-effectiveness theorem.

**Evaluated proposition.** Nonlinear representation complexity is justified by its declared use and operating regime — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.

**Original form.** A fit of several local dynamics is not an identified hybrid system until the claimed mode assignments, transition or partition law, and relevant regime coverage are supported separately.

**Original problem.** Latent clustering is mistaken for a physical mode ontology, or a theorem with observed switching is applied when modes are hidden or state-dependent.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Separate within-mode dynamics, mode assignment, mode count and switching law, and invoke each hybrid-identification result only under its actual mode-observation and trajectory assumptions.

**Claim class.** ASSUMPTION_OR_DOMAIN_CONDITION

**Bearer or subject.** A switched or hybrid model, including its mode variable and switching semantics

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Latent clustering is mistaken for a physical mode ontology, or a theorem with observed switching is applied when modes are hidden or state-dependent.

**Mechanism.** Separate observed mode labels from inferred labels; specify arbitrary, stochastic or state-dependent switching; test both within-mode dynamics and boundary/transition predictions.

**Mature or evolved form.** Separate within-mode dynamics, mode assignment, mode count and switching law, and invoke each hybrid-identification result only under its actual mode-observation and trajectory assumptions.

**Expected payoff.** Prevent invalid theorem transfer and detect mode confusion that aggregate error hides.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** FR003 gives the structural distinctions; FR004 proves a finite-sample result only with measured iid switching and other explicit conditions.

**Decision or consumer.** Choose hybrid model class and decide whether mode-sensitive control or diagnosis is justified.

**Alternative mechanisms.** A single local model covers all visited regimes, or known mode labels permit independent fits without learned switching.

**Reconciled mechanism and target distinctions.** A102 hybrid component becomes this row; its HMM probability-learning component belongs to FR04. B adds a 2025 observed-mode single-trajectory theorem, not a solution of arbitrary hidden switching.

**Reconciled shared content.** Unvisited or observationally indistinguishable modes cannot be uniquely recovered by repeating the same uninformative experiment.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Operating regimes switch, saturation/impact occurs, or a finite-sample switched-model guarantee is invoked.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A single local model covers all visited regimes, or known mode labels permit independent fits without learned switching.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Rácz–Petreczky–Daróczy: measured iid modes with positive probabilities, hidden continuous state, bounded/independent input and noise conditions, minimality and common quadratic contraction A_q^T P A_q < (gamma²/n_Q²)P with gamma<1. Recovery is up to similarity. Hidden or state-triggered switching falls outside this theorem.

**Environment and boundary.** FR004’s partially observed means hidden continuous state, not unobserved switching. Its recovered matrices are only up to similarity.

**Scope and exclusions.** Rácz–Petreczky–Daróczy: measured iid modes with positive probabilities, hidden continuous state, bounded/independent input and noise conditions, minimality and common quadratic contraction A_q^T P A_q < (gamma²/n_Q²)P with gamma<1. Recovery is up to similarity. Hidden or state-triggered switching falls outside this theorem.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Research-derived acceptance rule, not an imposed obligation. No universal standard or target authority is asserted. Any domain-specific authority must be supplied separately.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Record {mode observability, label semantics, mode count, switching law, within-mode data, transition coverage, realization equivalence, theorem hypotheses}. Preserve source/data/model versions and separate observed facts from assumptions.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Parent property ids.** None recorded.

**Tension ids.** ESI-RTN0033

**Predicate specifications.** **Predicate id.** ESI-RPR0079

**Property id.** ESI-RC-FR03

**Name and plain language claim.** A claimed hybrid-mode distinction has discriminating observation evidence

**Predicate kind.** ASSUMPTION_OR_DOMAIN_CONDITION

**Subject and argument signature.** ModeDistinction(F,S_required,observation,D,noise_bound)

**Variable domains and units.** F declared finite candidate switched/PWA models; S_required finite mode/transition set; inputs/outputs in declared physical units; noise_bound nonnegative in output units

**Quantifiers and scope.** For each mode/transition distinction actually needed by the consumer, within the explicitly enumerated candidate family; label permutations are equivalent unless externally grounded

**State trace event or model bearer.** hybrid candidate models, observation map and mode-conditioned traces

**Temporal and modal semantics.** Finite distinction claim for current modes/partition and observation regime; no unbounded behavioral-equivalence guarantee

**Assumptions.** Declared mode law (exogenous/Markov/partition), candidate family and error bound; observation protocol can expose the alleged distinction

**Applicability guard.** A mode identity, partition or regime-specific behavior is claimed from partial observations

**Expression or precise operational rule.** PASS only for the declared finite candidate class when observations/allowed probes distinguish every decision-relevant nonequivalent candidate and required modes have evidence; FAIL a unique-distinction claim if an explicit pair remains observationally identical but differs on the required behavior; UNKNOWN for unvisited modes, unbounded candidate search or unreliable assignments; INAPPLICABLE when only undifferentiated output prediction is claimed.

**Source of the expression.** **Type.** RESEARCHER_PROPOSED_ASSESSMENT

**Basis.** ESI-RS0037 §§II–III; this is not a theorem of general hybrid identifiability

**Observation or measurement map.** Map measurements and inputs to candidate mode-dependent outputs with the declared noise tolerance; inferred mode labels are not treated as independently observed truth

**Required evidence.** Candidate models, mode/partition definition including boundary assignment, observation/sensor map, required regimes and discriminating trace/probe records

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** Compare predicted observation sets under allowed inputs, accounting for label permutation and error bound; mark unvisited or inseparable candidates explicitly

**Decidability and approximation.** Finite explicitly enumerated candidates can be compared on specified experiments; arbitrary hybrid model identification/equivalence is not solved by this assessment

**Positive witness.** Constructed noise-free alternatives y=u and y=2u are distinguishable at u=1 if these are the declared competing modes; their physical names still need external grounding

**Counterexample or failure witness.** At u=0 those alternatives yield identical output; arbitrarily many repetitions there cannot identify the active mode. An unvisited mode can retain arbitrary dynamics.

**Unknown conditions.** Unknown candidate set, mode assignment, sensor map, switching law or noise bound; missing required mode/transition evidence

**Inapplicability conditions.** No mode/partition distinction is required; validate a bounded output predictor instead

**False positive and false negative risks.** False distinction from noise or sensor drift; false failure if an external mode sensor already supplies the needed information but was omitted

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Treat inferred labels as ground truth for evaluating the same inference; split one mode into many labels to inflate apparent structure

**Change invalidation rule.** New mode, altered partition/switching logic, sensor mapping or required input domain invalidates the distinction evidence

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Use known mode labels or a direct diagnostic sensor when cheaper; do not infer unused hidden distinctions

**Evidence ceiling.** Decision-relevant distinguishability within a declared finite family, not general unique hybrid realization

**Evaluated proposition.** A claimed hybrid-mode distinction has discriminating observation evidence

**Actual evaluation status.** EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** An observable latent representation can support its specified predictions without uniquely identifying physical hidden coordinates; rank-conditioned HMM guarantees and semantic anchors must be assessed separately.

**Claim class.** SEMANTIC_CORRESPONDENCE_OR_REFINEMENT

**Bearer or subject.** A specified HMM and its invoked observable-prediction guarantee, or a partially observed model and its proposed latent interpretation.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Prediction error is promoted into evidence that a latent coordinate equals a physical mechanism or internal state.

**Mechanism.** State the equivalence class preserved by observations, distinguish predictive quantities from latent interpretations, and demand independent interventions or measurements for the latter.

**Mature or evolved form.** An observable latent representation can support its specified predictions without uniquely identifying physical hidden coordinates; rank-conditioned HMM guarantees and semantic anchors must be assessed separately.

**Expected payoff.** Retain useful prediction while avoiding unjustified latent ontology.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** FR005 proves finite-horizon distribution learning under rank conditions; FR004 explicitly allows similarity transformations. Neither identifies physically named hidden variables.

**Decision or consumer.** Choose permissible claims and whether extra sensors/interventions are worth their cost.

**Alternative mechanisms.** The consumer only needs calibrated sequence predictions and does not use latent labels.

**Reconciled mechanism and target distinctions.** A contributes explicit HMM theorem premises and a rank-domain predicate. B contributes a semantic-correspondence predicate accepting either invariant predictions or independently anchored hidden quantities. Neither predicate replaces the other. The outer trigger is the union of the retained Hsu-invocation and latent-interpretation targets. Rank/positivity/sampling conditions are assessed as the named theorem warrant, and physical labels are not required to invoke that assessment.

**Reconciled shared content.** Prediction of observations and physical interpretation of latent state are different targets; similarity or permutation leaves observable behavior unchanged.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** The Hsu spectral guarantee is being claimed, including by a purely predictive HMM without semantic labels, or hidden-state models, encoders or HMMs are given semantic labels. Unestablished or violated theorem premises do not suppress assessment of an invoked guarantee.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** No Hsu spectral guarantee is invoked and no hidden-state semantic interpretation is being assessed. Calibrated observable prediction can be an adequate cheap route without physical labels, but an invoked Hsu guarantee still requires its own theorem-warrant assessment.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Hsu Condition 1: positive initial probabilities and full column rank of emission O and transition T for m hidden states. Theorem 6 bounds fixed-horizon observation-sequence L1 error under sample/conditioning conditions and independent sequences; stronger conditional KL result needs additional positivity. Do not infer physical coordinates or single-long-trajectory guarantees. These are conditions for the invoked theorem warrant, not prerequisites to assess the invocation. Independent semantic anchors are required only for an interpretation that needs them.

**Environment and boundary.** No unrestricted transfer from linear/HMM observability to arbitrary nonlinear or agent internals.

**Scope and exclusions.** Hsu Condition 1: positive initial probabilities and full column rank of emission O and transition T for m hidden states. Theorem 6 bounds fixed-horizon observation-sequence L1 error under sample/conditioning conditions and independent sequences; stronger conditional KL result needs additional positivity. Do not infer physical coordinates or single-long-trajectory guarantees.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Research-derived acceptance rule, not an imposed obligation. No universal standard or target authority is asserted. Any domain-specific authority must be supplied separately.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Record {predictive target, observation map, allowed state transformations, horizon, rank/conditioning, independent semantic anchors}. Preserve source/data/model versions and separate observed facts from assumptions.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Parent property ids.** None recorded.

**Tension ids.** ESI-RTN0034

**Explanation.** Physical priors can break symmetries; the limitation should not be mistaken for impossibility under all additional information.

**Failure of assumptions.** A known violation of a cited Hsu premise defeats that theorem warrant; it does not alone falsify observed predictive accuracy. Two admissible observationally equivalent realizations with different claimed meanings and no distinguishing evidence defeat the separately asserted unique-meaning claim.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Extra sensors and experiments for semantic anchoring; latent dimension selection and conditioning checks.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Changed sensors, policy, state dimension or semantic labeling invalidates the interpretation claim.

**Reconciled composition consequence.** FR03 mode evidence complements rather than proves latent meaning. FR23 agent-internal boundary shares nonuniqueness reasoning without inheriting an HMM theorem.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0090

**Strongest objection.** Physical priors can break symmetries; the limitation should not be mistaken for impossibility under all additional information.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: relabel the states of an HMM and permute transition/emission parameters; the output law is unchanged while an unanchored state name changes.

**Response or descendant form.** Use predictive-state semantics or add explicit physical constraints and anchor measurements, then reassess identifiability.

**Original form.** Minimize data residual plus a weighted prior/smoothness penalty.

**Original problem.** Small residuals can coexist with unstable or nonunique inverse solutions.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Distinguish existence, numerical stability, uniqueness of a regularized solution, well-posed posterior inference and identification of the external target; regularization or a prior may select a useful answer without adding distinguishing observations.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_ENGINEERING_CLAIM

**Bearer or subject.** An inverse problem, regularizer and target claim

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A unique smooth/minimum-norm optimizer is called the uniquely recovered physical object.

**Mechanism.** Expose the feasible data-equivalence class and the complete optimization problem, including domain, A, L, center and parameter; separate full-space rank reasoning from constrained existence/uniqueness and from physical target identification.

**Mature or evolved form.** Distinguish existence, numerical stability, uniqueness of a regularized solution, well-posed posterior inference and identification of the external target; regularization or a prior may select a useful answer without adding distinguishing observations.

**Expected payoff.** Stable numerical estimates without concealing what the data alone cannot determine.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Manual examples show numerical behavior, not an independently validated field payoff or universal error reduction. Hansen Eq.(2.39) gives unconstrained stacked least squares. For fixed A,L,b,x*,λ>0 on R^n, the kernel-intersection iff follows by finite linear algebra. Feasible-class identifiability and the CASE-B003 constrained-domain discriminators are separate constructed arguments.

**Decision or consumer.** Which inverse estimate or range can support a physical conclusion or downstream action.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Additional informative measurement; Constrained/set-valued estimate; Truncated SVD; Direct measurement; Use a target functional constant on the nullspace

**Reconciled mechanism and target distinctions.** A supplies finite deterministic Tikhonov/nullspace criteria. B supplies Bayesian posterior existence, Hellinger stability and approximation. These are complementary native claims and preserve different spaces, metrics and uncertainty meanings.

**Reconciled shared content.** A unique selected solution does not establish unique physical recovery. A target functional may already be identified although the full unknown vector is not.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Forward-map inversion is ill-conditioned, rank-deficient or prior-dependent.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** If the consumer needs only x1+x2 and A=[1,1], that sum is identified; no unique x vector or elaborate regularizer is needed.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** For fixed finite A,L,b,x*, lambda>0 and domain R^n, the unconstrained Tikhonov minimizer is unique iff ker(A) intersects ker(L) only at zero. Constrained domains require separate existence/uniqueness arguments. Target q must be constant on a nonempty feasible class. Bayesian results retain prior, likelihood/potential and regularity assumptions; no automatic frequentist coverage.

**Environment and boundary.** Mathematical inverse solution versus the real object and the chosen target functional.

**Scope and exclusions.** For fixed finite A,L,b,x*, lambda>0 and domain R^n, the unconstrained Tikhonov minimizer is unique iff ker(A) intersects ker(L) only at zero. Constrained domains require separate existence/uniqueness arguments. Target q must be constant on a nonempty feasible class. Bayesian results retain prior, likelihood/potential and regularity assumptions; no automatic frequentist coverage.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Record the exact objective and admissible domain, operator discretization, units/scaling, noise covariance, fixed penalty/center, λ-selection and tuning data; identify any separate constrained existence/uniqueness argument.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** Connects C0105 sparse priors, C0107 projection and C0109 known-physics inverse fitting; tension between stability and bias.

**Failure of assumptions.** A wrong penalty can stabilize the wrong answer; near-null directions remain practically unidentifiable.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Inspect nullspace/target first; a direct sum measurement avoids recovering every component

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Operator, noise regime, units, regularizer or requested target changes require a fresh sensitivity/equivalence assessment.

**Reconciled composition consequence.** FR06 causal action requires additional structural/intervention premises. FR17 physics priors do not cure inverse nonuniqueness. Root uncertainty rows preserve posterior versus feasible-set semantics.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0015

**Strongest objection.** Regularization can create persuasive precision by encoding an incorrect prior; small residuals and unique optima do not settle physical ambiguity.

**Known failures and misuses.** The same data admit (1,0),(0,1) and (.5,.5); choosing the minimum-norm vector cannot establish which physical vector generated them.

**Response or descendant form.** Disclose the prior and distinguish target functionals; vary the penalty/noise assumptions and collect a discriminating measurement if uniqueness matters.

**What changed and what did not.** A supplies finite deterministic Tikhonov/nullspace criteria. B supplies Bayesian posterior existence, Hellinger stability and approximation. These are complementary native claims and preserve different spaces, metrics and uncertainty meanings.

**Residual limits.** External model class and noise/prior correspondence can remain unknown. Seek a measurement outside the present nullspace or conduct prior/forward-model sensitivity for the actual target.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Demanding a unique full reconstruction when only a measured functional is needed adds avoidable machinery.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0006; ESI-RTN0007

**Retention status.** RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

**Retention rationale.** A unique selected solution does not establish unique physical recovery. A target functional may already be identified although the full unknown vector is not. A supplies finite deterministic Tikhonov/nullspace criteria. B supplies Bayesian posterior existence, Hellinger stability and approximation. These are complementary native claims and preserve different spaces, metrics and uncertainty meanings.

**Name and plain language claim.** Penalized uniqueness is distinguished from target identifiability

**Predicate kind.** MATHEMATICAL_MODEL_PROPERTY

**Subject and argument signature.** UniqueReg(A,L,lambda,b,x_star,D) and Identified(q,A,b,D)

**Variable domains and units.** A∈R^(m×n); L∈R^(p×n); b∈R^m; x,x*∈R^n; λ>0 with declared scaling; D⊆R^n; q has declared target units. The kernel iff test has guard D=R^n.

**Quantifiers and scope.** For fixed A,L,b,x*,λ>0, minimizing J(x)=||Ax-b||²+λ²||L(x-x*)||² over all x∈R^n has a unique minimizer iff ker(A)∩ker(L)={0}. Do not extend that iff to arbitrary D. Separately, for nonempty F_b={x∈D:Ax=b}, the target is identified iff q(x)=q(x′) for every x,x′∈F_b.

**State trace event or model bearer.** specified finite linear inverse model

**Temporal and modal semantics.** Static claims for a fixed objective, observation equation, center and admissible domain; full-space and constrained optimization are distinct cases

**Assumptions.** Finite real linear A,L, fixed b and center x*, fixed λ>0. The source stacked least-squares uniqueness test is restricted to unconstrained R^n; constrained D requires its own existence/uniqueness warrant. Target identification uses the declared nonempty feasible class and observation/noise interpretation.

**Applicability guard.** A linear regularized inverse claim is made

**Expression or precise operational rule.** Report optimization uniqueness and target identification separately. For D=R^n and fixed A,L,b,x*,λ>0, PASS uniqueness iff ker(A)∩ker(L)={0}; otherwise FAIL uniqueness. For constrained D, the full-space iff shortcut is INAPPLICABLE: use a separate domain-appropriate existence and uniqueness argument, with UNKNOWN when that argument is missing or unresolved. Separately PASS target identification only if nonempty F_b={x∈D:Ax=b} has constant q; FAIL if an explicit feasible equal-data pair has unequal q; UNKNOWN if the operator, domain, nonemptiness or equivalence class is unresolved. Forward prediction without an inverse target is INAPPLICABLE.

**Source of the expression.** **Type.** SOURCE_DEFINED_PLUS_RESEARCHER_RECONSTRUCTION

**Source.** ESI-RS0039 §2.7.1 Eq.(2.39) supplies unconstrained stacked least squares and a sufficient rank condition; the full-space iff and feasible-class target test are elementary linear-algebra reconstructions

**Observation or measurement map.** A maps physical parameter units to observations; q specifies the desired reported quantity

**Required evidence.** A,L,λ,b, fixed center x*, exact objective, admissible domain D, target q and noise/precision statement; a separate constrained existence/uniqueness argument when D≠R^n

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** First identify D and fixed objective data. Apply the full-space kernel-intersection iff only on R^n; for constrained D assess existence and uniqueness with its own argument. Independently establish the nonempty feasible data class and q constancy; report the two conclusions separately.

**Decidability and approximation.** The full-space rank test is finite linear algebra. General constrained existence/uniqueness and nonlinear target constancy require separate proofs or bounded analysis and may remain UNKNOWN.

**Positive witness.** For A=[1,1], q(x)=x1+x2 is constant across exact-data solutions; this target is identified

**Counterexample or failure witness.** For A=[1,1], b=1, the feasible vectors (1,0),(0,1),(.5,.5) fit equally; minimum norm selects (.5,.5) without identifying x1. Existing CASE-B003 also contains two analytical-only constrained-domain discriminators for misuse of the full-space iff.

**Unknown conditions.** Unknown operator/domain or feasible-class nonemptiness; unresolved constrained existence/uniqueness; noise tolerance without a declared compatible uncertainty set

**Inapplicability conditions.** The full-space uniqueness shortcut is inapplicable when D≠R^n, while feasible-class target identification can still apply. The whole inverse-target assessment is inapplicable to forward prediction without an inverse claim.

**False positive and false negative risks.** False unique claim from rank tolerance or applying the full-space test to a nonconvex domain; false rejection of a unique constrained minimizer or an identified target functional

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Reporting narrow optimizer curvature as total physical uncertainty

**Change invalidation rule.** Changes in A,L,b,λ,center x*,domain D,units,noise or q require reassessing the corresponding optimization or identification claim

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Inspect nullspace/target first; a direct sum measurement avoids recovering every component

**Evidence ceiling.** Uniqueness/stability within the specified inverse problem, not proof that the regularizer or forward model describes nature

**Evaluated proposition.** Penalized uniqueness is distinguished from target identifiability

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** **Steps.** Check applicability before substantive evaluation.; Bind the attribute record to actual versions and classify observed versus assumed components.; Apply the specific operational rule and inspect the stated counterexample class.; Return one outcome with the decisive evidence and remaining scope.

**Outcomes.** **Pass.** The stated mathematical property follows under verified assumptions, and any uniqueness claim is explicitly qualified or independently supported.

**Fail.** A stable regularized solution is claimed to prove uniqueness despite an exhibited observational nullspace or equivalent alternative.

**Unknown.** Forward-map hypotheses, prior sensitivity or approximation error are unverified.

**Inapplicable.** No inverse-recovery or stability claim is being made.

**Decidability and approximation.** A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.

**Positive witness.** FR006’s Hellinger-continuity result supports stability of a conditional posterior under its hypotheses.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** Constructed: y=theta1+theta2; a quadratic penalty selects a unique minimum, while infinitely many parameter pairs fit the same noise-free observation.

**Unknown conditions.** Forward-map hypotheses, prior sensitivity or approximation error are unverified.

**Inapplicability conditions.** No inverse-recovery or stability claim is being made.

**False positive and false negative risks.** False positive: Regularization-induced selection or posterior concentration is mistaken for data-determined uniqueness. False negative: Priors encode legitimate knowledge and can make an otherwise underdetermined decision useful.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. A well-posed posterior proves the true physical parameter is uniquely identified.

**Change invalidation rule.** Changed forward model, prior, noise model, discretization or target quantity requires renewed analysis.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Posterior computation and prior-sensitivity studies; infinite-dimensional discretization control can be substantial. Cheaper path: A directly observed, well-conditioned quantity can be estimated with a transparent low-dimensional model.

**Evidence ceiling.** Bayesian well-posedness does not itself validate the prior, likelihood, solver or physical forward model. Misspecified model classes can yield stable but wrong answers. FR006 proves posterior well-posedness and approximation results under stated hypotheses, not universal parameter recovery.

**Evaluated proposition.** Inverse-problem well-posedness and regularization are distinct from unique external recovery — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.

**Original form.** An intervention replaces a structural equation; an estimand is identified if all observationally compatible allowed models agree on it.

**Original problem.** A predictor valid under one data-generating policy can fail under intervention or changed confounding.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** An intervention functional is identified only when admissible causal models consistent with the evidence agree on that functional; predictive fit under an observed policy does not itself supply this agreement.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_ENGINEERING_CLAIM

**Bearer or subject.** A predictive dynamic model used for an intervention estimand

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Correlation, fit, state observability or invariant residuals are treated as sufficient proof of causal effects.

**Mechanism.** Define intervention semantics and the admissible causal model class; seek observationally equivalent models with different effects; use justified interventions, exclusions or adjustment conditions to remove that ambiguity.

**Mature or evolved form.** An intervention functional is identified only when admissible causal models consistent with the evidence agree on that functional; predictive fit under an observed policy does not itself supply this agreement.

**Expected payoff.** Prevent a policy change from exploiting a spurious predictive association while permitting justified intervention prediction.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** The inspected sources contain method demonstrations; no universal transfer from predictive performance to intervention accuracy is established. Pearl defines identification; ICP Theorem 1 controls false positive inclusion under valid tests; ObsNODE Theorem 4.3 is an assumption-heavy preprint causal-adjustment result.

**Decision or consumer.** Whether to forecast the effect of an action rather than merely the next observed value.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Randomized permitted intervention; Instrumental/structural design with valid assumptions; Set-valued partial identification; Remain within predictive use

**Reconciled mechanism and target distinctions.** A adds ICP false-inclusion control and the 2026 observable-neural causal hybrid. B develops earlier structural-equation semantics and explicit controlled-input alternatives. Preserve these routes without equating architectural observability to identified causal parameters.

**Reconciled shared content.** Observation and intervention have different semantics. A bounded predictor need not reconstruct an entire causal graph when no action/transport claim is made.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** The consumer changes an input/policy/mechanism or asks a counterfactual/causal question.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** If the consumer only predicts observations under the same supported policy, a causal graph is not mandatory; label the claim predictive.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Define the intervention, model class, population/horizon, observation map and needed consistency, overlap, confounding/invariance or controlled-input premises. ICP can return an empty selected set while honoring its coverage; it does not promise all true parents.

**Environment and boundary.** Specified causal estimand in specified population/regime; prediction of observed outcomes is a different evidential target.

**Scope and exclusions.** Define the intervention, model class, population/horizon, observation map and needed consistency, overlap, confounding/invariance or controlled-input premises. ICP can return an empty selected set while honoring its coverage; it does not promise all true parents.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Record who/what assigned inputs, temporal order, measured confounders, hidden-state assumptions, intervention targets and environment-selection process.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** C0102 state reconstruction, C0111 evaluation and C0112 guarantee transfer are prerequisites only when their actual assumptions are met; none substitutes for causal identification.

**Failure of assumptions.** Hidden confounding, target interventions that break invariance or lack of overlap can invalidate effect predictions despite good fit.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Use a predictive label when sufficient; collect the smallest permitted intervention distinguishing the disputed effect

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Changed policy, target population, intervention mechanism, observation history or confounding assumptions requires renewed identification analysis.

**Reconciled composition consequence.** FR22 forcing does not become manipulable/exogenous by being predictive; FR23 external agent behavior does not identify hidden intentions. Root control uses may obtain the necessary evidence by controlled inputs without compulsory causal-graph reconstruction.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0016

**Strongest objection.** Overly strong causal assumptions can relocate uncertainty out of the estimator; no predictive score verifies absence of hidden confounding.

**Known failures and misuses.** Executed observationally identical pair yields different do-effects. ObsNODE §7 separately acknowledges that clinical counterfactual accuracy lacks ground truth.

**Response or descendant form.** Keep structural assumptions explicit, exploit valid interventions/invariance, report partial or empty identification, and distinguish observable-state architecture from causal evidence.

**What changed and what did not.** A adds ICP false-inclusion control and the 2026 observable-neural causal hybrid. B develops earlier structural-equation semantics and explicit controlled-input alternatives. Preserve these routes without equating architectural observability to identified causal parameters.

**Residual limits.** Unobserved confounding or unavailable interventions can prevent identification. Exhibit compatible models with different Q or supply justified evidence excluding one; physical transfer of ObsNODE remains bounded.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A causal diagram used only as decoration adds no intervention evidence.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0007; ESI-RTN0009

**Retention status.** STRONGLY_RETAINED

**Retention rationale.** Observation and intervention have different semantics. A bounded predictor need not reconstruct an entire causal graph when no action/transport claim is made. A adds ICP false-inclusion control and the 2026 observable-neural causal hybrid. B develops earlier structural-equation semantics and explicit controlled-input alternatives. Preserve these routes without equating architectural observability to identified causal parameters.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Interpret sparse coefficient recovery relative to a specified coordinate map, function library, sufficient observed state, numerical error model and informative trajectories; test any structural claim on discriminating regimes.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_ENGINEERING_CLAIM

**Bearer or subject.** Sparse dynamic model selection from observed trajectories

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A concise fitted equation is called the law despite missing features, transformed coordinates, unobserved state or manifold-confined data.

**Mechanism.** Declare basis and coordinate units, assess informative variation, test off-training trajectories, and use weak residuals when derivative estimation dominates noise.

**Mature or evolved form.** Interpret sparse coefficient recovery relative to a specified coordinate map, function library, sufficient observed state, numerical error model and informative trajectories; test any structural claim on discriminating regimes.

**Expected payoff.** Obtain interpretable compact models when the system is sparse in an appropriate representation and the data distinguish terms.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** SINDy demonstrates selected dynamical examples and reports failures. Accessed WSINDy v3 gives ODE demonstrations but explicitly defers direct computational comparison with conventional SINDy. Weak identity follows integration by parts and source test-function assumptions; numerical quadrature and noisy nonlinear features still limit estimation.

**Decision or consumer.** Whether a selected equation supports prediction, interpretation or a designed experiment.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Known-family parameter estimation; Weak/integral regression; Coordinate discovery with separate validation; Non-sparse predictor; Additional measurements/transients

**Reconciled mechanism and target distinctions.** A105 sparse-recovery component maps here; its weak-form numerical mechanism maps FR08. B adds hard-nonlinearity/hidden-state benchmarks and corrects the claim that linear-in-coefficient regression cannot represent products: a product can be a dictionary column. A sparse prediction or structural claim activates assessment before state/library sufficiency is established. The prediction and structural-warrant targets retain separate outcomes; an unknown premise affects only the claim that needs it, and a known structural counterexample cannot become INAPPLICABLE.

**Reconciled shared content.** Sparsity is representation-dependent, and more data on an uninformative manifold cannot determine missing terms or hidden dynamics.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A selected sparse equation is claimed to explain or predict dynamics, including a physical or structural interpretation, whether observed-state sufficiency, library adequacy or numerical premises are established, unknown or contradicted.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Only a known fixed law is fitted directly, with no selected sparse explanation, prediction or discovery claim to assess. A fitted predictor without structural interpretation removes only the structural target; a claimed selected sparse predictor still receives its bounded validation assessment.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Keep feature/coefficient units, rank and scaling, derivative/integral error, initial states and sampled transients. For structural recovery, justify sufficient observed state, library representability at the claimed accuracy and distinguishing data. For bounded prediction, assess the observation, numerical and held-out criteria material to that declared envelope. These are warrant/outcome conditions, not invocation gates; identifiability in one library is not all-library or all-coordinate uniqueness.

**Environment and boundary.** Equation recovery within a representation/envelope; this can be an effective reduced law rather than a unique physical law.

**Scope and exclusions.** Keep feature/coefficient units, rank and scaling, derivative/integral error, initial states and sampled transients. Identifiability of one selected library is not all-library or all-coordinate uniqueness.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Store coordinate transform, units, dictionary terms, derivative/test functions, quadrature, thresholds, trajectory/initial-condition provenance and selection/validation separation.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** C0103 regularization, C0106 dictionary validation and C0111 independent evaluation interact; more library terms can reduce conditioning.

**Failure of assumptions.** An actual omitted-state/library counterexample that contradicts the advertised structure or required trajectory yields FAIL of that claim. An unproved or violated merely sufficient proof premise alone leaves the underlying claim UNKNOWN unless the evaluated target is explicitly that premise or warrant. A failed structural warrant does not automatically negate a directly checked bounded predictive result.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Use known-family estimation first when justified; weak integration trades derivative noise for quadrature/test-function design

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Changed dictionary, coordinates, sensing, sample rate or target transient/regime requires support selection and validation to be reconsidered.

**Reconciled composition consequence.** FR04 state correspondence and FR08 weak numerical control are independent premises for a structural conclusion. FR09 rejects promotion of the resulting sparse fit to unique law.

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** WSINDy explicitly modifies SINDy using weak/Galerkin machinery. It is a documented method descendant and import, not a universal successor replacing direct differentiation.

**Original terminology.** weak form; test function; integration by parts; generalized least squares

**Original form.** Integrating against suitable test functions can avoid pointwise differentiation of noisy data, but does not remove library error, observation insufficiency, quadrature error or tuning dependence.

**Original problem.** Noise amplification by numerical derivatives prevents useful coefficient recovery.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RGN0202

**Influence or relation class.** EXPLICIT_IMPORT

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Weak/integral formulations can reduce pointwise differentiation noise by moving derivatives to known test functions. Bounded weak-identity/error claims require their numerical and tuning conditions; recovery claims additionally require supported state, library and identifiability assumptions.

**Claim class.** ACCEPTANCE_OR_ASSURANCE_CONDITION

**Bearer or subject.** A weak-form dynamic regression procedure

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Noise amplification by numerical derivatives prevents useful coefficient recovery.

**Mechanism.** Transfer derivatives from measured trajectories to known smooth test functions, include boundary conditions, and account for correlated residuals from overlapping windows.

**Mature or evolved form.** Weak/integral formulations can reduce pointwise differentiation noise by moving derivatives to known test functions. Bounded weak-identity/error claims require their numerical and tuning conditions; recovery claims additionally require supported state, library and identifiability assumptions.

**Expected payoff.** More stable sparse estimation under supported noise and sampling conditions.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** FR009 supplies the method and numerical demonstrations; its threshold choices partly use true coefficients, limiting claims of blind deployment.

**Decision or consumer.** Choose derivative estimation or a weak formulation and its tuning protocol.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Accurate derivatives or low-noise dense measurements already support a simpler regression.

**Reconciled mechanism and target distinctions.** A105 is decomposed because numerical error reduction and sparse structural distinguishability have different tests. B contributes a distinct weak-form attribute/predicate and the ground-truth threshold-information limitation. Weak-form use for noisy derivative regression invokes the existing predicate before state sufficiency is known. NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY and RECOVERY_WARRANT are explicit targets within that predicate, with no new property or registry row. State/library sufficiency remains material to recovery but is not automatically a premise of a bounded integral-identity/error statement.

**Reconciled shared content.** Both inputs identify a concrete numerical response to derivative-noise amplification and explicitly deny that it solves structural identifiability.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Weak forms are used for a noisy derivative-regression problem and their numerical adequacy or an associated recovery warrant is assessed. State sufficiency, library adequacy and numerical premises may be established, unknown or violated; they are not invocation gates.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** No noisy derivative-regression problem is present or weak forms are not used. Accurate derivatives or low-noise dense measurements may support a cheaper direct regression; missing state or an inadequate library is not a non-trigger for an asserted weak-form recovery claim.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** For NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY, establish the regularity, boundary treatment, quadrature resolution, noise/covariance control and permitted tuning information needed by the stated weak-identity/error claim. RECOVERY_WARRANT additionally needs justified state/observation sufficiency, library adequacy and informative data for the defended recovery scope. These conditions are assessed after invocation; numerical control cannot supply missing structural information.

**Environment and boundary.** Noise robustness is not structural identifiability or hidden-state reconstruction.

**Scope and exclusions.** Test functions must meet integration-by-parts boundary/regularity conditions; quadrature must resolve the data and relevant transitions. Overlap-induced residual correlation needs treatment. A threshold chosen using the true minimum nonzero coefficient is unavailable to a blind learner.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Research-derived acceptance rule, not an imposed obligation. No universal standard or target authority is asserted. Any domain-specific authority must be supplied separately.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Record {test functions, support windows, boundary treatment, quadrature, measurement noise, residual covariance, tuning information}. Preserve source/data/model versions and separate observed facts from assumptions.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Parent property ids.** None recorded.

**Tension ids.** ESI-RTN0036

**Explanation.** Weak integration can smooth away fast events or merge regimes.

**Failure of assumptions.** An actual identity, boundary/quadrature-error or tuning-access violation contradicts the selected numerical claim; for RECOVERY_WARRANT, an actual omitted-state/library structural counterexample or established violation of its explicitly required support criterion defeats that warrant. A false merely sufficient proof premise alone does not falsify the underlying solution or recovered law.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Window/test-function selection, numerical quadrature and covariance modeling.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Changed sample spacing, noise dependence, window length or library requires renewed calibration.

**Reconciled composition consequence.** FR07 supplies library and state premises; FR03 mode boundaries can limit window choice. Better integration does not imply causal validity or physical-law uniqueness.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0094

**Strongest objection.** Weak integration can smooth away fast events or merge regimes.

**Known failures and misuses.** A threshold selected from the smallest true coefficient is not available in a blind unknown-law task; reproducing that score does not establish blind applicability.

**Mechanism.** Actual useful mechanism is constrained search over expressions; identification additionally requires discriminating observations, justified coordinates and a clearly defined equivalence oracle.

**Mature or evolved form.** The universal inference from minimum symbolic complexity or a sparse low-error fit alone to the unique generating physical law is false; qualified recovery needs independently warranted representation and distinguishing evidence.

**Expected payoff.** Readable/testable hypotheses without treating readability as proof.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** SRBench separates black-box prediction and known-form symbolic recovery; its accessed version lacks real-world first-principles-known datasets. LLM-SRBench adds oracle and transformed-task limits. The two scalar laws have identical observed zero trajectories yet different nonzero trajectories; this exactly refutes the universal implication.

**Decision or consumer.** Whether to interpret a symbolic equation physically or use it as a compact predictor/hypothesis.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Report equivalence class; Targeted experiment; Known-family fit; Non-symbolic predictor if interpretation is not needed; Dimensional/structural constraints with justification

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Nonintrusive projection-based reduction is the native tradition; fitting an operator does not make OpInf a descendant of every DMD/Koopman algorithm.

**Original terminology.** Nonintrusive operator inference; intrusive projected operators; polynomial reduced dynamics

**Original form.** Infer reduced operators from projected full-state trajectories rather than accessing full-model operators.

**Original problem.** A black-box simulator supplies trajectories but not operators needed for intrusive projection.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RBR0012

**Influence or relation class.** HYBRIDISATION; EXPLICIT_IMPORT

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** ESI-RS0047

**Locator.** Introduction; §3.2

**Specific claim.** Inference is explicitly compared with intrusive projection of the full model.

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Least squares and projection precede this method; no claim that it is the origin of all operator learning.
