### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Operator inference estimates the specified structured reduced operators from projected full-state data under rank and numerical assumptions; its convergence theorem does not promise arbitrary fixed-small-order physical recovery.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_ENGINEERING_CLAIM

**Bearer or subject.** A learned reduced polynomial operator and the source full simulator

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Convergence to a projection is described as exact physical-law recovery or guaranteed accuracy at any fixed small reduced dimension.

**Mechanism.** Project full state data into a declared basis, form a polynomial least-squares design and compare inferred coefficients with the intrusive reduced target under stated limits.

**Mature or evolved form.** Operator inference estimates the specified structured reduced operators from projected full-state data under rank and numerical assumptions; its convergence theorem does not promise arbitrary fixed-small-order physical recovery.

**Expected payoff.** Construct reduced models when full operators are unavailable but appropriate trajectories are available.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Source examples use a linear climate model and polynomial tubular reactor; they demonstrate feasibility of nonintrusive reduction, not independent validation of the full physics. Theorem 1 compares inferred and intrusive operators under full-rank and discretization conditions and allows n→N; it does not give a universal fixed-small-rank result.

**Decision or consumer.** Whether a reduced surrogate is accurate/useful enough for repeated simulation, analysis or later control validation.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Intrusive projection when operators accessible; Black-box output surrogate; Direct full simulator; Regularized constrained operator inference with separate proof

**Reconciled mechanism and target distinctions.** A explicitly preserves the existential reduced-dimension/time-step quantifiers. B labels the same native method domain-specific. Both describe a conditional theorem, so the canonical status reflects assumption sensitivity rather than averaging favorable labels.

**Reconciled shared content.** The reference target is the intrusive projection of a supplied full model, not automatically the external plant.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Full state trajectories and polynomial structural information exist, while full operators are inaccessible or expensive to use.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** If the full model is cheap and rarely queried, or an adequate reduced model is already available, operator inference may have no lifecycle benefit.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Known polynomial structure, projection basis, full-state snapshots, consistent derivative/time approximation and full-column-rank design. For every epsilon the theorem permits suitable n<=N and sufficiently small time step, potentially n approaching N; it is not for every prechosen small n.

**Environment and boundary.** The reduced projection of a specified mathematical full model, not nature itself.

**Scope and exclusions.** Known polynomial structure, projection basis, full-state snapshots, consistent derivative/time approximation and full-column-rank design. For every epsilon the theorem permits suitable n<=N and sufficiently small time step, potentially n approaching N; it is not for every prechosen small n.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Record full model/version, state access, projection basis, input trajectories, derivative estimator, step size, design rank and downstream validation.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** C0103 regularization can alter bias/target; C0112 quantifiers prevent fixed-rank overclaim; C0111 validates surrogate behavior independently.

**Failure of assumptions.** Rank deficiency, missing state access, basis truncation or derivative bias can prevent the theorem conditions or accurate useful reduced dynamics.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Use direct simulation or existing surrogate when reuse cannot amortize inference/validation

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Full model, reduced basis/dimension, structural terms, time step or input regime changes require new rank and surrogate checks.

**Reconciled composition consequence.** FR10 finite linear closure and FR13 polynomial reduction have no general implication in either direction. CL19 carries the exact target/quantifiers; RT04 allows an existing full simulator for a few queries.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0019

**Strongest objection.** The projection reference may itself be biased or inaccurate, and an existence theorem can require a dimension that removes the hoped-for computational savings.

**Known failures and misuses.** A fixed tiny basis can omit dynamically important directions regardless of sample count; the theorem’s existence of a larger n does not certify that tiny model.

**Response or descendant form.** Keep projection/truncation and inference error separate, report rank/numerical conditions, and compare finite useful reduced models against an adequate baseline.

**What changed and what did not.** A explicitly preserves the existential reduced-dimension/time-step quantifiers. B labels the same native method domain-specific. Both describe a conditional theorem, so the canonical status reflects assumption sensitivity rather than averaging favorable labels.

**Residual limits.** No universal stable tiny-order/noisy-data guarantee or external-plant validation follows. Assess rank/conditioning, truncation and held-out projected/full-model error at the actual chosen order.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Operator-learning terminology does not create value when a direct simulator already answers the few required queries.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0006; ESI-RTN0009

**Retention status.** ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE

**Retention rationale.** The reference target is the intrusive projection of a supplied full model, not automatically the external plant. A explicitly preserves the existential reduced-dimension/time-step quantifiers. B labels the same native method domain-specific. Both describe a conditional theorem, so the canonical status reflects assumption sensitivity rather than averaging favorable labels.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Finite physics-residual minimization alone does not universally establish the differential equation throughout its domain or the physical truth of the supplied operator family.

**Claim class.** UNIVERSAL_CLAIM_ADMITTED_FOR_FALSIFICATION

**Bearer or subject.** Finite collocation loss and a claimed physical law/solution

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Constraint residual, optimization convergence, PDE solution and physical correspondence are collapsed.

**Mechanism.** The actual useful mechanism is known-physics regularization or hard parameterization plus data; a finite soft residual is not a universal certificate.

**Mature or evolved form.** Finite physics-residual minimization alone does not universally establish the differential equation throughout its domain or the physical truth of the supplied operator family.

**Expected payoff.** Retained bounded form can combine sparse data and justified physics; universal form has no demonstrated payoff.

### Genealogy

**Original terminology.** symbolic regression; scientific equation discovery; LLM hypothesis generation; test-time adaptation

**Original form.** LLMs can generate useful equation hypotheses, but a discovery claim must distinguish remembered formulas, data-supported novelty, predictive fit, symbolic equivalence and evaluator error.

**Original problem.** Known benchmark equations or model-based judges inflate apparent discovery; useful predictions are mistaken for structural truth.

**Mature or evolved form.** Evaluate bounded task recovery, novelty/generalization and a data-dependent discovery mechanism separately, attaching actual exposure, prior tools, evaluator reliability and resource use to each proposition.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Preserve actual information access during agentic model/code search, evaluate a frozen result independently for an independent-generalization claim, and distinguish reproducibility of that exported model from repeatability of the stochastic search process.

**Bearer or subject.** An agent-controlled identification workflow

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A nominally held-out test is visible in logs, or a reproducible final model is treated as proof that the search process is reproducible and unbiased.

**Mechanism.** Bind the selected claim and actual information access, freeze/version the final executable artifact and evaluate its named bounded result. For independent generalization, insulate fresh final evaluation from selection. For repeated-search claims, record agent/tool/prompt versions, selection rules, run variation and total costs, and assess repeated searches separately from executing one saved model.

**Mature or evolved form.** Preserve actual information access during agentic model/code search, evaluate a frozen result independently for an independent-generalization claim, and distinguish reproducibility of that exported model from repeatability of the stochastic search process.

**Claim target rules.** **Bounded final artifact.** **Target.** The specified frozen model achieves the directly observed named benchmark result or satisfies a stated execution/training-repeatability criterion on the declared data and environment.

**Pass.** Reliable versioned execution and correctly computed metrics establish the stated bounded result; repeatability is checked to the extent actually claimed. Fully disclosed exposed-benchmark selection is compatible with this PASS.

**Fail.** Actual execution, metric or repeatability evidence contradicts the named bounded criterion.

**Unknown.** The artifact, data, relevant runtime/training procedure, metric or required repeatability evidence is missing or unreliable.

**Limit.** No independent generalization, repeated-search reproducibility, universal superiority or general labor saving follows.

**Independent generalization.** **Target.** The evaluation evidence warrants the specifically claimed independent prospective-generalization conclusion.

**Pass.** Final selection is fixed before a fresh evaluation whose data/results are insulated from selection, and the evaluation supports the claimed scope, inferential unit, horizon and criterion.

**Fail.** Known test-result access contradicts the asserted independence, or a valid target-matched evaluation contradicts the advertised performance criterion. Exposure FAILs independence warrant, not the truth of all possible generalization.

**Unknown.** Access, freeze chronology, evaluator reliability, target population or required generalization evidence is unresolved.

**Limit.** An honest exposed-benchmark result belongs to BOUNDED_FINAL_ARTIFACT; prompts forbidding use do not establish inaccessible information.

**Repeated search reproducibility.** **Target.** Repeated searches under the declared pipeline, version/resource conditions and run population meet the advertised reproducibility or outcome-distribution criterion.

**Pass.** Appropriate repeated-search runs and versioned process/resource records establish that criterion, including claimed run variation.

**Fail.** Actual repeated-search evidence contradicts the criterion, or artifact-only repetitions are falsely represented as completed repeated-search trials. The latter is failure of evidence warrant; it does not prove that repeated search could never reproduce.

**Unknown.** Only a saved artifact or insufficient repeated-search/process evidence is available and the missing repeated-run evidence is honestly acknowledged.

**Limit.** Execution of the same frozen artifact is not another stochastic search; repeated-search results do not establish independent generalization without that target’s separate evaluation boundary.

**Evaluation priority rule.** Check the agent/claim context, then select the exact target before applying any test-isolation or repeated-run condition. If the target itself is unspecified, the judgment is UNKNOWN. A decisive applicable contradiction or established misrepresentation of the selected warrant yields FAIL; established target-specific evidence yields PASS; otherwise missing material evidence yields UNKNOWN. Unasserted broader targets cannot veto a bounded PASS, and a bounded PASS cannot establish them.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Judge a model against a stated consumer, loss, horizon and operating envelope; small discrepancy in an unrelated norm cannot certify the decision.

**Bearer or subject.** A model together with a specified prediction, diagnosis, explanation or control decision.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A model selected solely by training MSE is used for high-bandwidth control without phase-error or robustness analysis.

**Mechanism.** Translate the decision into relevant outputs, frequencies, horizons and admissible errors; compare model and alternatives under that loss. Retain uncertainty where actions differ across compatible models.

**Mature or evolved form.** Fix the consumer/criterion and preserve contrary cases; retain a cheaper model when its relevant error is acceptable.

**Expected payoff.** Avoid spending on irrelevant fidelity and avoid accepting a precise model for the wrong decision.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Primary analytical control example establishes that error metrics can reverse adequacy; no general productivity effect size established.

**Decision or consumer.** A model is proposed for use or transfer to a new controller, regime or prediction horizon.

**Alternative mechanisms.** A coarse gain/sign model may suffice for a limited regulator or screening decision. A full state reconstruction is unnecessary when all compatible models support the same action.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Additional modeling is justified only by a decision-relevant benefit under explicit consequences, uncertainty and lifecycle cost, compared with feasible cheaper alternatives.

**Claim class.** QUALITATIVE_ASSESSMENT

**Bearer or subject.** Comparison of modeling options for one decision; no mathematical objective automatically legitimizes the decision.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Model size or accuracy is maximized without evaluating the decision it improves or the work required to maintain it.

**Mechanism.** Compare expected loss plus acquisition, computation, review, maintenance and retirement cost over a declared horizon, subject to non-tradable feasibility/authority constraints.

**Mature or evolved form.** Treat missing cost/benefit evidence as unknown; use sensitivity analysis and a cheap baseline instead of assuming every explicit model pays.

**Expected payoff.** Can avoid negative-value modeling and identify cases in which extra fidelity is economically material.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Published economic reasoning and scenario calculations; general realized causal gains across model classes remain unestablished.

**Decision or consumer.** A choice is being made to build, enlarge, maintain or replace a model.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Direct measurement, bounded rule, lookup table or no new model meets the decision tolerance.

**Canonical common and distinct content.** All three compare a model/representation or update against feasible alternatives for a common consumer. A has explicit lifecycle costs and selected twin cases; B0042 concerns representation value and B0068 emphasizes changed predictive/decision losses. Retain those contexts, not three independent properties.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A choice is being made to build, enlarge, maintain or replace a model.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Direct measurement, bounded rule, lookup table or no new model meets the decision tolerance.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Costs and consequences are commensurate or separately constrained.; Reuse horizon and uncertainty are explicit.; The alternative is feasible and evaluated fairly.

**Environment and boundary.** Comparison of modeling options for one decision; no mathematical objective automatically legitimizes the decision.

**Scope and exclusions.** No conversion of ordinal judgments into arbitrary additive utility, no universal ROI estimate, no equation that authorizes an intervention.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Feasibility and authority are external constraints, not benefits to trade away.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Cost observations/estimates with provenance, consumer loss, horizon, baseline and uncertainty.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Profile id.** ESI-RPF035

**Dependence.** The complete profile supplies the bearer and required questions; this record’s rule and exclusions specialize it.

**Failure of assumptions.** ESI-RCA0055: stipulated decision loss falls from10 to8, but upkeep5 makes total loss-plus-cost13 exceed the baseline10; this is constructed arithmetic, not measured validation performance.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Detailed investment analysis itself has a cost; simple dominance or a bounded pilot can settle low-stakes cases.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Retire when consumer value disappears, maintenance exceeds plausible benefit or a simpler adequate option dominates.

**Response or descendant form.** Keep the economic model conditional and compare ranges; conduct a bounded discriminating evaluation if the decision warrants it.

**What changed and what did not.** Treat missing cost/benefit evidence as unknown; use sensitivity analysis and a cheap baseline instead of assuming every explicit model pays.

**Residual limits.** No general empirical cost-benefit result for arbitrary identification artifacts.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Direct measurement, bounded rule, lookup table or no new model meets the decision tolerance.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** No general empirical cost-benefit result for arbitrary identification artifacts. Cost and field studies support bounded examples, with partial body access; no universal return or universal waste conclusion follows.

**Transferability limits.** No conversion of ordinal judgments into arbitrary additive utility, no universal ROI estimate, no equation that authorizes an intervention.

**Unverified or open questions.** No credible consequence model, baseline, horizon or total cost estimate.

**Next discriminator.** For an actual candidate use, obtain Cost observations/estimates with provenance, consumer loss, horizon, baseline and uncertainty. Then test: Within feasible authorized options and a declared horizon, prefer added model m only if its evidence-supported reduction in decision loss exceeds its incremental lifecycle cost, or it satisfies a separately required feasibility constraint unavailable to the baseline. If intervals overlap materially, report UNKNOWN rather than forcing a ranking.

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Behavioral systems formulation inspected in Willems 2007; earlier relational/network ideas are acknowledged but no first-invention claim is made.

**Original terminology.** behavior; manifest and latent variables; tearing, zooming, linking

**Original form.** System as a set of admissible trajectories and interconnected physical variables.

**Original problem.** Input-output arrows can impose structure absent from physical interconnection.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RGN0289

**Influence or relation class.** CRITICAL_RESPONSE

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** ESI-RS0213

**Locator.** pp.46–59

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Ashby is a conceptual antecedent only; no direct transmission from Ashby to every later algorithm is asserted.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** When shared physical constraints do not justify a global directed partition, retain a relational model and make any input-output selection explicit.

**Claim class.** FORMAL_RECONSTRUCTION

**Bearer or subject.** A model and its physical/abstract variable boundary.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Spurious causality or lost interconnection constraints caused by forcing directed arrows.

**Mechanism.** Define manifest behavior through relations; preserve latent and initial-condition semantics while choosing a representation.

**Mature or evolved form.** A purpose-bound alternative to input-output modeling, with correspondence obligations.

**Expected payoff.** Avoid losing behavior important to the consumer.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Source hydraulic/constraint examples and constructed offset counterexample demonstrate the failure mechanism; no general measured cost saving.

**Decision or consumer.** Physical modeler or assessor comparing representations.

**Alternative mechanisms.** A justified input-output model; A small constraint system; A direct measured relationship

**Canonical common and distinct content.** B preserves the modeling choice between an implicit relation and a directed input-output representation. A numerical implicit-equation property does not cover the same external-versus-internal variable partition or elimination mechanism.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Interconnection or transformation where shared variables/latent constraints matter.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A verified unilateral sensor-actuator interface may already justify input-output form.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Declared variable domains and units; Common trajectory/initial-condition interpretation

**Environment and boundary.** The selected physical or mathematical boundary; no universal social ontology.

**Scope and exclusions.** Does not settle causal-inference disputes or identify undocumented software by itself.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** NOT_APPLICABLE: mathematical/descriptive modeling gives no permission to intervene.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Record origin and physical meaning of each equation and variable.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** Can complement physical constraints; conflicts with unexamined universal input-output partitioning.

**Failure of assumptions.** A symbolically equivalent equation can describe the wrong physical variables.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Constraint bookkeeping and elimination can be expensive; preserve only needed correspondence.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-enter when interconnection, variables or consumer changes.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0106

**Strongest objection.** A more general relational form can make computation and intervention interpretation harder without improving a particular decision.

**Known failures and misuses.** Treating every implicit equation as identified physics; Using a broad critique of causality to deny legitimate directional interfaces

**Response or descendant form.** Keep input-output and port-based forms where their added structure is justified.

**What changed and what did not.** Representation choice becomes explicit; empirical correspondence remains unproved by syntax.

**Residual limits.** General behavior equivalence can be intractable; model boundaries are still choices.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A diagram is optional; preserved constraints are the mechanism.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0041

**Retention status.** DOMAIN_SPECIFIC

**Retention rationale.** Strong physical-modeling mechanism with no basis for universally replacing all other representations.

### Predicates, witnesses and evaluation

**Predicate specifications.** **Predicate id.** ESI-RPR0124

**Property id.** ESI-RC-RT09

**Name and plain language claim.** Preservation of manifest behavior by an explicit representation

**Predicate kind.** SEMANTIC_CORRESPONDENCE_OR_REFINEMENT

**Subject and argument signature.** equivalent_manifest_behavior(R, R_prime, W, L, domain)

**Variable domains and units.** w in declared trajectory space W; latent l in L; physical units attached to components

**Quantifiers and scope.** For every admissible manifest trajectory w in the specified domain, existence of a latent witness is equivalent in both representations.

**State trace event or model bearer.** equivalent_manifest_behavior(R, R_prime, W, L, domain)

**Temporal and modal semantics.** A relation over complete specified trajectories, not a statement inferred merely from finite samples.

**Assumptions.** Common variables/units, domain and initial-condition semantics; The relation being compared is explicitly supplied

**Applicability guard.** A representation transformation claims to preserve manifest behavior.

**Expression or precise operational rule.** For all w in domain: (exists l: R(w,l)=0) iff (exists l_prime: R_prime(w,l_prime)=0).

**Source of the expression.** Researcher-written predicate using the behavioral notion in ESI-RS0213; not claimed to be a quotation or universal decision procedure.

**Observation or measurement map.** Bind each manifest variable to a sensor, physical terminal, or declared abstract variable; keep that correspondence separate from equation equivalence.

**Required evidence.** Both relations, latent-variable domains, initial conditions and a proof/counterexample at the claimed scope.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** **Pass.** A sound argument establishes both inclusions in the declared model/domain.

**Fail.** An admissible trajectory satisfies exactly one representation.

**Unknown.** Only finite tests or an incomplete elimination/proof are available.

**Inapplicable.** No behavior-preservation claim is made; e.g. a deliberately approximate predictor.

**Decidability and approximation.** Linear algebraic finite models permit exact elimination; general nonlinear differential behavior equivalence has no single automatic decision procedure asserted here.

**Positive witness.** For R: y=l and l=2u, eliminating l gives y=2u in the same real domain.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** ESI-RCA0114: matching velocities loses a position offset; derivative-only equality is weaker.

**Unknown conditions.** Missing initial condition, unit interpretation, latent domain or proof of either inclusion.

**Inapplicability conditions.** A deliberately lossy abstraction with a different, separately stated error/adequacy contract.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** A solver returns one branch and hides other solutions.

**False negative.** Different equations are rejected merely because their syntax differs.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** An empty or accidentally inconsistent behavior makes inclusion tests vacuous; prove a relevant nonempty witness.

**Change invalidation rule.** Recheck after changing observation map, variable domain, constraint, initial condition or intended preserved claim.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Use exact algebra only on the decision-relevant slice; a declared approximate map may be cheaper.

**Evidence ceiling.** Equality in a declared mathematical model is not empirical truth, causality, normative authority or complete system recovery.

## ESI-RC-RT10 — Target-specific data informativity and a common decision

### Identity

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** 2019 preprint/2020 journal informativity formulation explicitly rooted in identification and behavioral data methods.

**Original terminology.** informativity; systems consistent with data

**Original form.** Universal property/decision over the compatible-system set.

**Original problem.** Persistent excitation sufficient for unique identification may exceed what a particular analysis/control task needs.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RGN0290

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** ESI-RS0214

**Locator.** Introduction and Definition 1

**Source id.** ESI-RS0215

**Locator.** Introduction

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** The authors explicitly build on earlier informativity; no claim that data-based control began in 2019.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Require information sufficient for the actual objective; a common valid decision can exist despite nonunique models.

**Claim class.** SOURCE_DEFINED_THEORETICAL_RESULT

**Bearer or subject.** A dataset, model class, compatible set and stated analysis/control objective.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Unnecessary insistence on recovering every parameter; nominal-only decisions that ignore remaining models.

**Mechanism.** Quantify over all compatible systems, with a single common decision where needed.

**Mature or evolved form.** Exact, bounded-error or probabilistic formulations with different explicit assumptions.

**Expected payoff.** A bounded certificate can avoid unnecessary unique reconstruction.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Theorem and exact counterexample show possibility; no general field-cost reduction established.

**Decision or consumer.** Assessor of a defined stability, controllability or control objective.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Identify a suitable model and uncertainty set; Use a conservative known controller; Collect a discriminating experiment

**Canonical common and distinct content.** B retains a separate common-controller/property decision across a nonempty compatible-system set, rather than requiring unique identification first. CL01/03 explain equivalence/information but do not alone prove that one controller works for every compatible model.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A defined decision may be common to all remaining explanations.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A fully known adequate plant/controller may need no new data-driven method.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** **Model certificate.** A defined nonempty set of models consistent with the declared exact/noisy data and one fixed quantified property; control uses one common realizable K within the mathematical decision class.

**External system application.** Separate evidence must establish actual-system inclusion, measurement/noise assumptions and physical realizability before transferring the model certificate.

**Environment and boundary.** Model-family and objective specific; scalar analytical example noiseless LTI with full state.

**Scope and exclusions.** No universal claim that persistent excitation is unnecessary, or that LQR/constraints need the same information as stabilization.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** NOT_APPLICABLE to mathematical inference; collecting data or changing feedback needs independent authorization.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Bind measurements, noise model, model class, objective and implemented policy.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** Depends on informative observations and honest uncertainty; can bypass unique parameter identification for certain consumers.

**Failure of assumptions.** A certificate on the wrong compatible set can be false about the physical plant.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Set construction, robust optimization, solver margins and data collection; infeasibility may be conservatism.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Changed objective, state access, noise or policy requires a new information claim.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0107

**Strongest objection.** Compatible-system validity and tractable shared certificates can be more demanding than the direct label suggests.

**Known failures and misuses.** Vacuous empty-set reasoning; Per-model rather than common policy; Transferring noiseless rank arguments to noisy full-rank matrices

**Response or descendant form.** Noisy input-output and probability-bounded extensions add noise/prior/margin hypotheses.

**What changed and what did not.** Data access assumptions expand; coverage of the real system remains essential.

**Residual limits.** Field calibration, nonlinear misspecification and exploration safety need separate evidence.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** The compatible set and decision certificate matter; a full exported plant model is not always needed.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0042

**Retention status.** ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE

**Retention rationale.** Strong bounded theorem refutes a universal unique-identification prerequisite; external coverage remains sensitive.

### Predicates, witnesses and evaluation

**Predicate specifications.** **Predicate id.** ESI-RPR0125

**Property id.** ESI-RC-RT10

**Name and plain language claim.** Data are informative for the specified property or common controller

**Predicate kind.** MATHEMATICAL_MODEL_PROPERTY

**Subject and argument signature.** informative(D, Sigma, P) or stabilizing_gain(D,Sigma,K)

**Variable domains and units.** D is finite exact input-state data in the LTI example; Sigma a class; K a feedback gain with input/state units

**Quantifiers and scope.** For all S in nonempty Sigma_D, P(S); for control, there exists one K such that for all S in Sigma_D, P(S,K).

**State trace event or model bearer.** informative(D, Sigma, P) or stabilizing_gain(D,Sigma,K)

**Temporal and modal semantics.** The data are finite; the stability claim is an infinite-time property of every compatible model under fixed feedback.

**Assumptions.** **Model certificate.** A defined nonempty set of models consistent with the declared exact/noisy data and one fixed quantified property; control uses one common realizable K within the mathematical decision class.

**External system application.** Separate evidence must establish actual-system inclusion, measurement/noise assumptions and physical realizability before transferring the model certificate.

**Applicability guard.** A bounded analysis/control objective can be evaluated over a compatible-system set.

**Expression or precise operational rule.** Sigma_D != empty and Sigma_D subseteq Sigma_P; for stabilization, exists K: forall (A,B) in Sigma_D, spectral_radius(A+B*K)<1.

**Source of the expression.** Informativity definition source-defined in ESI-RS0214 Definition 1; explicit nonemptiness guard and four-outcome wrapper are researcher additions.

**Observation or measurement map.** Bind recorded inputs/states, time alignment and noise to the matrices defining consistency.

**Required evidence.** Declared class, data, verified consistency/noise assumptions and a common certificate; external inclusion evidence assessed separately. State whether the selected claim is MODEL_CERTIFICATE or EXTERNAL_SYSTEM_APPLICATION; do not use missing empirical mapping to negate an exact model proof.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** **Pass.** A sound proof/certificate establishes the quantified claim on a nonempty compatible set.

**Fail.** For a fixed K, an admissible compatible model violates the property; existential failure needs a complete impossibility result.

**Unknown.** A nonempty compatible set or common quantified certificate is unestablished; a failed solver search alone does not show impossibility.

**Inapplicable.** No well-defined common property/decision or outside the selected model family.

**Decidability and approximation.** The inspected noiseless LTI state-feedback case has rank/LMI characterizations; no universal solver asserted for arbitrary models or properties.

**Positive witness.** ESI-RCA0112: a=b+1/2 for all consistent scalar models and K=-1 makes the closed-loop coefficient 1/2.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** If all-zero observations leave arbitrary unstable uncontrollable scalar models admissible, the desired stabilization certificate need not exist.

**Unknown conditions.** A nonempty compatible set or common quantified certificate is unestablished; a failed solver search alone does not show impossibility. Unknown physical meaning, actual-system membership or measurement assumptions leaves EXTERNAL_SYSTEM_APPLICATION unknown, not a proved MODEL_CERTIFICATE.

**Inapplicability conditions.** An interpretive institutional account lacking a defined system class and decision property.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** Exclude the real plant by an unjustified noise bound, or use a different K for each model.

**False negative.** Demand unique identification even though one common K exists.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Empty model sets make universal inclusion vacuous; per-model controllers do not establish a common controller.

**Change invalidation rule.** Reassess after changing model class, data policy, observation map, noise description, objective or actuator envelope.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** A small model set or direct certificate may be cheaper than unique identification; robust feasibility can also be more conservative/computationally costly.

**Evidence ceiling.** A conditional mathematical guarantee; no authority, safety during learning, optimality for another objective or external plant validity follows.

**Claim target evaluation rules.** **Model certificate.** **Pass.** A sound proof/certificate establishes the quantified claim on a nonempty compatible set.

**Fail.** For a fixed K, an admissible compatible model violates the property; existential failure needs a complete impossibility result.

**Unknown.** A nonempty compatible set or common quantified certificate is unestablished; a failed solver search alone does not show impossibility.

**Inapplicable.** No well-defined common property/decision or outside the selected model family.

**External system application.** **Pass.** The model certificate passes and independent evidence establishes all material correspondence, inclusion, noise and realization premises for the particular external claim.

**Fail.** A reliable external witness contradicts the asserted correspondence, membership or application consequence.

**Unknown.** External inclusion/correspondence or another material transfer premise is unestablished, even if the mathematical certificate is proved.

**Inapplicable.** Only the explicitly mathematical model theorem is asserted; no external application claim is requested.

**Evaluated proposition.** AS_EXPLICITLY_NAMED_IN_ORIGINAL_SPECIFICATION

**Actual evaluation status.** EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

## ESI-RC-RT11 — Physical structural closure under compatible port interconnection

### Identity

**Property id.** ESI-RC-RT11

**Property name.** Physical structural closure under compatible port interconnection

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_SYSTEM_IDENTIFICATION

**Property families.** PHYSICAL_STRUCTURE; COMPOSITION; GUARANTEE

**Record kind.** QUALIFIED_MECHANISM

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** ESI-RS0219; ESI-RS0220

**Member path.** EVOLVED_SYSTEM_IDENTIFICATION_PROPERTY_LEDGER.json

**Json pointer.** /properties/63

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Port modeling and geometric control tradition; inspected 2007 original composition proof and 2020 contributor exposition.

**Original terminology.** Dirac structure; composition; port-Hamiltonian system

**Original form.** Power-conserving interconnection closes the specified model class.

**Original problem.** Modular physical modeling with algebraic constraints and energy exchange.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RGN0289

**Influence or relation class.** DOCUMENTED_FORK_OR_DESCENDANT

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** ESI-RS0220

**Locator.** Introduction acknowledges earlier proofs and 2002 preliminary versions

**Source id.** ESI-RS0219

**Locator.** §1

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** No claim this is a descendant of statistical identification; it is a physical-modeling constraint imported where appropriate.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Within a justified port-Hamiltonian model, compatible power-conserving interconnection preserves the structural class.

**Claim class.** SOURCE_DEFINED_THEORETICAL_RESULT

**Bearer or subject.** Component Dirac structures, storage and dissipative relations.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Invalid modular assembly or lost energy accounting.

**Mechanism.** Compose dual port relations with common effort/opposite flow and sum component storage.

**Mature or evolved form.** Typed structural closure, distinguished from well-posedness, identification and deployment safety.

**Expected payoff.** Reusable structural reasoning about physical components.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Original proof establishes closure; no general comparative engineering-cost claim.

**Decision or consumer.** Modeler needing energy/passivity structure across a physical interconnection.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Direct circuit/force/flow equations; Validated input-output model; Local conservation check

**Canonical common and distinct content.** B has a specific Dirac/port-structure closure result absent as an original A property. It is a positive narrow theorem, not a counterexample to A rejection of arbitrary local-PASS composition.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Physical components have justified compatible port structure.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Small conservation equations suffice when no modular closure consumer exists.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Both component relations are Dirac structures for the specified pairing; Shared spaces and signs match; Constant finite-dimensional case is used

**Environment and boundary.** The exact interconnection/model class; measured correspondence not supplied by the theorem.

**Scope and exclusions.** No arbitrary software-property composition theorem; no all-context stability guarantee.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** NOT_APPLICABLE: mathematical relation provides no change authority.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Component equations, units, port orientation, storage and dissipative sign convention.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** Complements physical priors but can conflict with a representation that loses shared constraints.

**Failure of assumptions.** Mispaired ports or wrong signs destroy the intended energy argument.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Constructing geometry, constraints and valid physical correspondences; unnecessary for some simple consumers.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Reassess after model reduction or changes to ports/storage/interconnection.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0108

**Strongest objection.** The physical meaning and sufficiency of energy variables are not guaranteed by elegant structural closure.

**Known failures and misuses.** Treating passivity as asymptotic stability; Ignoring algebraic/initial compatibility; Claiming arbitrary properties compose because ports do

**Response or descendant form.** Separate structural closure, DAE/regularity checks, stability arguments and external validation.

**What changed and what did not.** Mathematical modularity is strengthened; the physical modeling burden remains.

**Residual limits.** Nonlinear control may encounter the dissipation obstacle; not all desired energy shaping is realizable.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Geometry is useful when it eliminates repeated structural proof; otherwise direct constraints may be cheaper.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0041

**Retention status.** DOMAIN_SPECIFIC

**Retention rationale.** A rigorous narrow composition mechanism, preserved without universal transfer.

### Predicates, witnesses and evaluation

**Predicate specifications.** **Predicate id.** ESI-RPR0126

**Property id.** ESI-RC-RT11

**Name and plain language claim.** Closure under the specified power-conserving interconnection

**Predicate kind.** MATHEMATICAL_MODEL_PROPERTY

**Subject and argument signature.** dirac_closure(D_A,D_B,F_shared,pairing)

**Variable domains and units.** Finite-dimensional real dual spaces; flow/effort coordinates with compatible power units

**Quantifiers and scope.** For all component elements satisfying common effort and opposite inward flow, the existentially projected relation is self-orthogonal.

**State trace event or model bearer.** dirac_closure(D_A,D_B,F_shared,pairing)

**Temporal and modal semantics.** Algebraic structure claim at the chosen parameter/state setting; not an all-time empirical safety statement.

**Assumptions.** Both component relations are Dirac structures for the specified pairing; Shared spaces and signs match; Constant finite-dimensional case is used

**Applicability guard.** A physical-model composition explicitly uses compatible port-Hamiltonian/Dirac representations.

**Expression or precise operational rule.** D_A o D_B = {(f1,e1,f3,e3): exists(f2,e2), (f1,e1,f2,e2) in D_A and (-f2,e2,f3,e3) in D_B}; check D_A o D_B=(D_A o D_B)^perp.

**Source of the expression.** ESI-RS0220 equation (13) and Theorem 3; evaluation wrapper researcher-defined.

**Observation or measurement map.** Correspond port variables and sign conventions to actual component terminals separately from the algebraic proof.

**Required evidence.** Component structures, common pairing, interconnection equations and a symbolic/verified linear-algebra closure argument. State whether the selected claim is MODEL_CERTIFICATE or EXTERNAL_SYSTEM_APPLICATION; do not use missing empirical mapping to negate an exact model proof.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** **Pass.** The model’s composed relation is a Dirac structure under the stated pairing.

**Fail.** The asserted structure/interconnection violates isotropy or dimension in the specified model.

**Unknown.** The model structures, pairing, rank/isotropy or the applicable theorem hypotheses are unestablished; physical correspondence is assessed separately.

**Inapplicable.** The components are not asserted to belong to this class.

**Decidability and approximation.** Exact finite-dimensional linear algebra is decidable; a state-dependent extension or DAE well-posedness is a separate claim.

**Positive witness.** ESI-RCA0113 correct orientation cancels internal power; the source theorem gives full structural closure beyond this scalar calculation.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** ESI-RCA0113 wrong orientation adds 12 units of internal power in the constructed port pair.

**Unknown conditions.** The model structures, pairing, rank/isotropy or the applicable theorem hypotheses are unestablished; physical correspondence is assessed separately. Unknown physical meaning, actual-system membership or measurement assumptions leaves EXTERNAL_SYSTEM_APPLICATION unknown, not a proved MODEL_CERTIFICATE.

**Inapplicability conditions.** A learned software protocol or unconstrained statistical predictor with no energy-port representation.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** Conflating zero power on a few points with maximal isotropy or field passivity.

**False negative.** Rejecting an equivalent structure expressed in different dual coordinates.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Zero trajectories alone satisfy power checks; a complete subspace argument is required.

**Change invalidation rule.** Recheck after port-sign/unit changes, new components, altered pairing or structural reduction.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** A local conservation equation can be cheaper; full geometry is justified only by a consumer of structural closure.

**Evidence ceiling.** Class closure and energy accounting in a model; not identification, empirical adequacy, asymptotic stability or authority.

**Claim target evaluation rules.** **Model certificate.** **Pass.** The model’s composed relation is a Dirac structure under the stated pairing.

**Fail.** The asserted structure/interconnection violates isotropy or dimension in the specified model.

**Unknown.** The model structures, pairing, rank/isotropy or the applicable theorem hypotheses are unestablished; physical correspondence is assessed separately.

**Inapplicable.** The components are not asserted to belong to this class.

**External system application.** **Pass.** The model certificate passes and independent evidence establishes all material correspondence, inclusion, noise and realization premises for the particular external claim.

**Fail.** A reliable external witness contradicts the asserted correspondence, membership or application consequence.

**Unknown.** External inclusion/correspondence or another material transfer premise is unestablished, even if the mathematical certificate is proved.

**Inapplicable.** Only the explicitly mathematical model theorem is asserted; no external application claim is requested.

**Actual evaluation status.** EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

## ESI-RC-RT12 — Rejected universal superiority of direct or model-free control

### Identity

**Property id.** ESI-RC-RT12

**Property name.** Rejected universal superiority of direct or model-free control

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_SYSTEM_IDENTIFICATION

**Property families.** CRITICISED_PROMOTION; MODEL_VALUE

**Record kind.** REJECTED_CANDIDATE

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** ESI-RS0218

**Canonical origin.** RECONCILED_INPUT_PROPERTY_NOT_NEW_EMERGENT_PROPERTY

**Canonical ancestry.** **Input alias.** B

**Archive sha256.** d34d1cd02f637d13713f7973b63fb2d90ea52860a09037d2963613a39549d34d

**Member path.** EVOLVED_SYSTEM_IDENTIFICATION_PROPERTY_LEDGER.json

**Json pointer.** /properties/64

**Original id.** ESI-C0076

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** A research-admitted overgeneralization exposed by modern direct/indirect comparisons; not attributed to a specific author as an endorsed slogan.

**Original terminology.** direct and indirect data-driven control

**Original form.** Prefer a direct method universally because it omits explicit identification.

**Original problem.** Avoid mismatch between fitting and control objectives.

**Branch ids.** ESI-RGN0290

**Influence or relation class.** RETROSPECTIVE_ANALOGY_ONLY

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** ESI-RS0218

**Locator.** §§III–VI

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** The universal slogan is the researcher’s adversarial candidate, not a quotation from the cited authors.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Candidate under criticism: omission of an explicit model guarantees lower cost or superior control across tasks.

**Claim class.** CRITICISED_UNIVERSAL_PROMOTION

**Bearer or subject.** A comparative method-choice claim.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Identification effort or objective mismatch, as claimed by the promotion.

**Mechanism.** Purported removal of a modeling step; actual formulations may encode identification in regularization.

**Mature or evolved form.** NO_GENERAL_PROPERTY: retain formulation-specific comparison and ESI-RC-RT10’s bounded alternative.

**Expected payoff.** Purported universal efficiency/performance gain.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Not supported generally; source comparisons and relaxation analysis give contrary/context-dependent evidence.

**Decision or consumer.** Method selector.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Qualified direct design; Identification then control with useful uncertainty; Hybrid/control-oriented fitting; Retain a simpler known method

**Canonical common and distinct content.** B separately examines the claimed superiority of avoiding an explicit model. Preserve direct/indirect regularization, relaxation and cost tradeoffs, and distinguish no named parametric model from absence of modeling assumptions.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A universal adoption claim is based on method labels.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A bounded demonstrated direct method needs no refutation of all indirect alternatives.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Task class and ordering specified; Valid comparator and matched information/tuning access

**Environment and boundary.** Exact comparator, task class, data and loss.

**Scope and exclusions.** Rejection is not a verdict against the entire direct-control family.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** NOT_APPLICABLE: comparative evidence supplies no authorization.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Full method and benchmark/tuning provenance, including failed trials.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** Conflicts with evidence showing noise, bias and computational trade-offs.

**Failure of assumptions.** Unmatched comparisons make the universal ranking uninterpretable.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Complex data constraints and regularizers may exceed a compact model’s cost.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Retire universal promotion; re-enter only as a specified bounded comparison.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ESI-RCR0109

**Strongest objection.** Direct formulations can have implicit identification, noisy vacuity, larger data requirements and unfavorable variance.

**Known failures and misuses.** Counting absence of a model file as absence of assumptions; Advertising a numerical gain as universal field superiority

**Response or descendant form.** Specific regularizers, noise bounds and hybrid objective formulations.

**What changed and what did not.** Useful direct methods survive; universal ranking does not.

**Residual limits.** Complete fair cross-domain costs remain unsettled.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Remove the universal label-based preference; keep actual matched comparisons.

**Internal tension ids.** ESI-RTN0042

**Retention status.** REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED

**Retention rationale.** A universal candidate has a concrete contrary comparison and no general supporting theorem.

### Predicates, witnesses and evaluation

**Predicate specifications.** **Predicate id.** ESI-RPR0127

**Property id.** ESI-RC-RT12

**Name and plain language claim.** Universal superiority from the direct/model-free label

**Predicate kind.** EMPIRICAL_REGULARITY_HYPOTHESIS

**Subject and argument signature.** universally_dominates(direct_method,indirect_method,declared_task_class,loss,cost)

**Variable domains and units.** Tasks in a fixed class; paired methods using comparable information; loss/cost with declared units

**Quantifiers and scope.** For every admissible task, direct loss/cost is no worse under the declared ordering.

**State trace event or model bearer.** universally_dominates(direct_method,indirect_method,declared_task_class,loss,cost)

**Temporal and modal semantics.** Universal comparative hypothesis; a finite contrary task can refute it, finite favorable tasks cannot establish it.

**Assumptions.** Task class and ordering specified; Valid comparator and matched information/tuning access

**Applicability guard.** An advocate asserts universal direct-method superiority.

**Expression or precise operational rule.** For all tasks t in T: direct(t) dominates_or_equals indirect(t) under the predeclared order; one valid violating t refutes the assertion.

**Source of the expression.** Researcher reconstruction of a criticized universal claim, not a source-endorsed theorem.

**Observation or measurement map.** Bind task outcomes to implementations, data, tuning, noise and consumer loss; count failures and costs.

**Required evidence.** A complete universal argument for PASS, or a valid comparative countercase for FAIL.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** **Pass.** Only a sound argument for the entire stated class; no such result is established here.

**Fail.** A valid task in the stated class reverses the asserted dominance.

**Unknown.** Only favorable case studies or incomparable budgets are supplied.

**Inapplicable.** The claim is only a bounded feasibility result or no universal comparison is made.

**Decidability and approximation.** No general finite empirical decision procedure for an unrestricted universal class; falsification is asymmetric.

**Positive witness.** A bounded exact-data equivalence may establish equal solutions for its own formulations; it cannot witness this unrestricted superiority claim.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** ESI-RS0218 §V-D: under the paper’s noisy LTI comparison, the direct method degrades more than the specified indirect method.

**Unknown conditions.** Missing baseline code, tuning budget, task membership, uncertainty or cost.

**Inapplicability conditions.** A researcher explicitly claims one bounded useful direct construction without comparative superiority.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** Compare a tuned direct method to a knowingly misspecified/undertuned baseline.

**False negative.** A failure of one formulation is generalized to all direct methods.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Select a task denominator after seeing results or omit infeasible/noisy cases.

**Change invalidation rule.** New methods or changed budgets require a new bounded comparison; existing counterexample still refutes the old universal statement.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Compare the cheapest adequate qualified methods; do not run broad benchmarks merely to decide a small local task.

**Evidence ceiling.** Rejection of the universal promotion, not rejection of direct data-driven control.

**Evaluated proposition.** AS_EXPLICITLY_NAMED_IN_ORIGINAL_SPECIFICATION

**Actual evaluation status.** EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.
